title: Green Climate Fund Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group 2027–2030: Call for Nominations for Indigenous Peoples Representatives
summary: The Green Climate Fund (GCF) has opened a call for nominations for its Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group (IPAG) for the 2027–2030 term , providing an opportunity for Indigenous Peoples representatives to contribute to dialogue, coordination, and engagement between Indigenous Peoples, the Green Climate Fund, and its partners on climate action and climate finance. For the 2027–2030 term, the GCF is seeking nominations to fill one vacancy in each of four regions: Africa, Eastern Europe and Central Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, and the Pacific . The nomination process is specifically designed as an Indigenous Peoples-led self-selection process , meaning nominations are expected to come through relevant Indigenous Peoples institutions, bodies, organizations, networks, and regional Indigenous Peoples caucuses. The call is particularly relevant to Indigenous Peoples organizations and representatives working on climate action, environmental issues, Indigenous Peoples rights, sustainable development, climate finance, community development, and related areas . Nomination deadline: 9 October 2026 About the Green Climate Fund Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group The Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group (IPAG) was established under the Green Climate Fund s Indigenous Peoples Policy to strengthen coordination and engagement between Indigenous Peoples and the Green Climate Fund and its partners. The group provides a mechanism through which Indigenous Peoples perspectives can be brought into the GCF s work. Its membership consists of Indigenous Peoples representatives from regions of developing States where the Green Climate Fund may fund activities. Rather than being an ordinary employment position, IPAG membership is part of the GCF s broader institutional approach to Indigenous Peoples participation and engagement. The current call follows recommendations arising from the eighth meeting of the Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group , after which the GCF Secretariat began the process of filling vacancies for the next 2027–2030 term. What Is the Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group? The Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group is a mechanism for strengthening interaction between the Green Climate Fund and Indigenous Peoples. This is particularly significant in the context of climate action because Indigenous Peoples and their communities are frequently closely connected to land, forests, water, biodiversity, natural resources, and ecosystems that are affected by climate change and climate-related interventions. Through IPAG, Indigenous Peoples representatives can participate in a structured advisory mechanism connecting Indigenous Peoples perspectives with the GCF and its partners. The group therefore provides an avenue for Indigenous Peoples institutions and representatives to contribute perspectives relevant to climate action, inclusion, environmental sustainability, and the interests and concerns of Indigenous Peoples in developing regions. Regional Vacancies for the 2027–2030 Term For the 2027–2030 IPAG term, the Green Climate Fund has identified four regional vacancies . There is one vacancy in each of the following regions : 1. Africa Indigenous Peoples institutions, bodies, organizations, networks, and regional Indigenous Peoples caucuses in Africa may submit nominations for the African regional vacancy. The nominee should be an Indigenous Peoples representative from a developing State where the GCF may fund activities . 2. Eastern Europe and Central Asia The second vacancy is for the Eastern Europe and Central Asia region. Relevant Indigenous Peoples institutions and organizations in this region may nominate an appropriate Indigenous Peoples representative who meets the requirements and considerations established in the IPAG Terms of Reference. 3. Latin America and the Caribbean The third vacancy covers Latin America and the Caribbean. Indigenous Peoples institutions, organizations, networks, and regional caucuses may participate in the self-selection process by submitting qualified nominations for this regional position. 4. Pacific The fourth vacancy is for the Pacific region. Indigenous Peoples organizations and institutions from eligible developing States in the Pacific may submit nominations for consideration. The GCF notes that where no eligible nomination is received from one of these four regions, the Secretariat may consider eligible nominations from underrepresented sub-regions or groups , consistent with advice from the Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group. Who Can Be Nominated? This opportunity is specifically focused on Indigenous Peoples representatives rather than applicants from the general public. The nominee should be a representative from an Indigenous Peoples institution, organization, body, network, or related structure in an eligible developing State where the Green Climate Fund may fund activities. Importantly, individuals do not simply submit a personal application independently. The nomination must come through an appropriate Indigenous Peoples institution, body, or organization. The nominating organization must also formally confirm that the individual has been nominated or endorsed by the organization s head or designated focal point. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to individuals who already have an established connection with Indigenous Peoples organizations or representative structures. What Experience Should the Nominee Demonstrate? The nomination must include a statement demonstrating how the nominee satisfies the criteria and factors for IPAG membership contained in the group s Terms of Reference. The nomination should also include a short CV or biography highlighting the nominee s experience and contributions that are relevant to areas such as: Indigenous Peoples issues Climate action Environmental issues Climate-related development Community-level initiatives Indigenous Peoples participation Related areas of relevance to the work of the Green Climate Fund The GCF specifically requests that the nominee s relevant experience and contributions be clearly presented. This means that a generic CV may not be sufficient on its own. The information submitted should help demonstrate the nominee s connection to Indigenous Peoples issues and/or climate action and explain why the person is appropriate for representation on the Advisory Group. Nomination Must Come From an Indigenous Peoples Organization One of the most important aspects of this call is that it is an organization-led nomination process . Individuals interested in being considered should therefore first establish whether an eligible Indigenous Peoples institution, organization, body, network, or regional caucus is able and willing to formally nominate or endorse them. The nominating organization is responsible for providing information about itself and the nominee and for confirming that the nomination is formally supported. The organization must identify the region for which the nomination is being submitted. Information Required From the Nominating Organization The Green Climate Fund has specified the information that must accompany each nomination. 1. Information about the nominating organization The submission should include: The name of the Indigenous Peoples institution, body, or organization. Contact details of the organization. The region for which the nomination is being submitted. This information allows the GCF to establish the institutional source of the nomination and the relevant regional context. 2. Information about the nominee The submission must provide: The nominee s full name. The nominee s contact details. Email address. Telephone number. The nominee s information should be accurate and current because the nomination process may involve subsequent communication with the individual and the nominating organization. 3. Formal confirmation of nomination or endorsement The nomination must include confirmation from the head or designated focal point of the nominating Indigenous Peoples institution, body, or organization . This confirmation should establish that the nominee has been formally nominated or endorsed by the organization. This is an important distinction because the opportunity is not structured as an open individual application. 4. Statement demonstrating eligibility and suitability The nominating organization must provide a statement demonstrating how the nominee meets the criteria and factors to be considered for IPAG membership as established in the Terms of Reference. This statement should therefore go beyond simply saying that the person is experienced. It should connect the nominee s experience, knowledge, representation, and contributions to the requirements and considerations for IPAG membership. 5. Short CV or biography The nomination should include a short CV or biography of the nominee. The GCF specifically asks that this document highlight the individual s: Experience relating to Indigenous Peoples issues; Contributions to Indigenous Peoples communities or organizations; Experience in climate action; Relevant experience in related areas. A strong biography should therefore make the nominee s relevant experience immediately clear rather than focusing primarily on unrelated professional achievements. 6. Additional endorsements Endorsements from other Indigenous Peoples institutions, bodies, or organizations within the respective region are highly encouraged . Although the GCF does not state that these additional endorsements are mandatory, they can form part of the regional self-selection process and demonstrate broader institutional support for the nominee. Organizations considering a nomination may therefore wish to explore whether additional Indigenous Peoples organizations within their region are willing to provide endorsements. How the Indigenous Peoples-Led Self-Selection Process Works The call is based on an Indigenous Peoples-led self-selection process . This means that the selection mechanism is designed to involve Indigenous Peoples institutions and representative structures in identifying nominees for the regional vacancies. The process is therefore different from a conventional recruitment exercise in which individuals compete for a job by submitting applications directly to an employer. The GCF is specifically asking relevant Indigenous Peoples institutions, bodies, organizations, networks, and regional Indigenous Peoples caucuses to submit nominations. The regional dimension is also important. Each of the four listed regions has one vacancy, and nominations should identify the region for which the nomination is being submitted. What Do IPAG Members Do? The detailed IPAG Terms of Reference describe the group s role and functions, membership arrangements, competencies and factors to be considered, the self-selection process, working arrangements, and provisions relating to revision and termination of the Terms of Reference. The Terms of Reference therefore provide the principal framework for understanding the responsibilities and expectations associated with IPAG membership. Potential nominees and nominating organizations should review the Terms of Reference carefully before preparing a submission. The GCF s announcement specifically directs prospective nominators to the Terms of Reference when demonstrating how a nominee meets the criteria and factors considered for IPAG membership. Is IPAG Membership a Paid Position? No. IPAG members serve on a voluntary and non-remunerated basis . This means that the opportunity should not be treated as a salaried employment position or paid consultancy. However, the GCF indicates that where in-person participation is required, travel-related arrangements may be supported in accordance with applicable GCF policies and procedures . This distinction is important: the membership itself is voluntary and unpaid, but certain travel-related arrangements associated with required in-person participation may receive support under applicable GCF rules. How Often Do IPAG Members Meet? IPAG members can expect to participate in: Two in-person meetings each year Monthly online meetings Additional online meetings where specific activities require them The frequency of participation means that nominees should be prepared to make a sustained commitment throughout the 2027–2030 term. The opportunity is therefore not simply an honorary designation. It involves ongoing participation in the group s work. Working Language The working language of the Green Climate Fund is English . Consequently, nominees should be able to participate in the group s activities within this working-language environment. Organizations preparing nominations should take this into account when identifying and supporting nominees. Duration of the Appointment The call concerns the 2027–2030 term of the Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group. This means that nominees are being considered for participation in the Advisory Group during this multi-year period rather than for a short-term event or one-time consultation. The expected meetings and activities described by the GCF indicate that members should be prepared for continued engagement throughout their term. Important Deadline The deadline for submitting nominations is: 9 October 2026 Nominations must be sent to: IPAGnomination@gcfund.org The Green Climate Fund s official announcement specifies that nomination submissions must reach this email address no later than 9 October 2026 . Organizations should therefore allow sufficient time to identify the nominee, obtain the required organizational confirmation, prepare the supporting statement, compile the nominee s CV or biography, and obtain any additional endorsements they wish to include. How to Prepare a Strong Nomination Organizations interested in submitting a nomination should carefully organize their materials before sending them. Step 1: Identify the relevant regional vacancy First determine whether the nomination relates to: Africa; Eastern Europe and Central Asia; Latin America and the Caribbean; or the Pacific. The nominating organization should clearly identify the region for which the nomination is being submitted. Step 2: Identify an appropriate Indigenous Peoples representative The nominee should have a clear connection to Indigenous Peoples representation and relevant experience. Organizations should consider the individual s experience with Indigenous Peoples issues, climate action, environmental matters, community engagement, and other areas relevant to the IPAG mandate. Step 3: Review the IPAG Terms of Reference Before preparing the nomination statement, the organization should review the official IPAG Terms of Reference. The Terms of Reference explain the role and functions of IPAG, membership, competencies and factors to be considered, the self-selection process, working arrangements, and other institutional provisions. This review is particularly important because the GCF requires the nomination to include a statement demonstrating how the nominee meets the relevant criteria and factors. Step 4: Prepare the nominee s CV or biography The CV or biography should focus attention on experience and contributions relevant to: Indigenous Peoples; climate action; environmental issues; community development; Indigenous representation; and related areas. Relevant achievements should be presented clearly and in a way that demonstrates the nominee s connection to the purpose of the Advisory Group. Step 5: Obtain formal organizational endorsement The organization s head or designated focal point should formally confirm the nomination or endorsement. This confirmation should be included in the submission. Step 6: Consider additional regional endorsements The GCF highly encourages endorsements from other Indigenous Peoples institutions, bodies, or organizations in the relevant region. Where appropriate, organizations may therefore seek additional endorsements to demonstrate broader regional support. Step 7: Submit before the deadline The completed nomination should be sent to IPAGnomination@gcfund.org no later than 9 October 2026 . Organizations should avoid leaving the submission until the final day because obtaining organizational confirmation and additional endorsements may require coordination with multiple people. Why This Opportunity Is Significant for Indigenous Peoples Representatives The IPAG nomination process provides a structured avenue for Indigenous Peoples representatives to participate in engagement with one of the major international institutions working on climate finance. The Green Climate Fund is focused on mobilizing and delivering climate finance for developing countries, and its work includes climate-related investments and partnerships across developing regions. The Fund currently reports activities across Africa, Asia and the Pacific, Eastern Europe, Central Asia and the Middle East, and Latin America and the Caribbean. The IPAG mechanism specifically recognizes the importance of Indigenous Peoples participation in this broader climate-finance context. For Indigenous Peoples organizations, therefore, the nomination process is an opportunity to put forward representatives who can contribute perspectives and experience relating to Indigenous Peoples and climate action. Who Should Consider This Opportunity? This call is particularly relevant to: Indigenous Peoples institutions; Indigenous Peoples organizations; Indigenous Peoples representative bodies; Indigenous Peoples networks; regional Indigenous Peoples caucuses; Indigenous Peoples representatives with experience in climate action; Indigenous Peoples representatives working on environmental issues; Indigenous Peoples advocates involved in climate and sustainable-development discussions; and eligible Indigenous Peoples representatives from developing States where the GCF may fund activities. It is important to emphasize that the call is not a general application opportunity open to anyone interested in climate change . The nomination must come through a relevant Indigenous Peoples institution, body, or organization, and the nominee must be an Indigenous Peoples representative from an eligible developing State. Regional and Geographic Eligibility The call specifically identifies four regions: Africa, Eastern Europe and Central Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, and the Pacific. The nominee should come from a developing State where the Green Climate Fund may fund activities. This means that geographic eligibility is tied to both the four regional vacancies and the GCF s framework concerning developing States where it may finance activities. The GCF s announcement provides a link to its countries and regions information for determining the relevant geographic context. Key Facts at a Glance Opportunity Details Opportunity Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group (IPAG) 2027–2030 Organization Green Climate Fund (GCF) Opportunity type Indigenous Peoples advisory/governance nomination Term 2027–2030 Vacancies Four regional vacancies Africa One vacancy Eastern Europe and Central Asia One vacancy Latin America and the Caribbean One vacancy Pacific One vacancy Nominees Indigenous Peoples representatives Geographic focus Developing States where GCF may fund activities Who submits Indigenous Peoples institutions, bodies and organizations Selection approach Indigenous Peoples-led self-selection process Membership Voluntary and non-remunerated Meetings Two in-person meetings annually and monthly online meetings Working language English Travel Travel-related arrangements may be supported for required in-person participation under applicable GCF policies Additional endorsements Highly encouraged Deadline 9 October 2026 Submission email IPAGnomination@gcfund.org Important Documents to Review The Green Climate Fund has published two principal documents associated with this call: Main Call for Nominations – provides the details of the 2027–2030 nomination process, regional vacancies, nomination requirements, and submission deadline. IPAG Terms of Reference – provides the framework covering the role and functions of IPAG, membership, competencies and factors to be considered, self-selection, working arrangements, and other provisions. Potential nominators should review both documents carefully before preparing their submission. Conclusion The Green Climate Fund Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group 2027–2030 call for nominations provides an institutional pathway for Indigenous Peoples representatives to contribute to engagement between Indigenous Peoples, the Green Climate Fund, and its partners. The opportunity is particularly distinctive because it is not structured as a conventional job, fellowship, scholarship, or individual application. Instead, it uses an Indigenous Peoples-led nomination and self-selection process , with relevant Indigenous Peoples institutions, bodies, organizations, networks, and regional caucuses playing a central role. Four regional vacancies are available for the upcoming term, covering Africa, Eastern Europe and Central Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, and the Pacific . Nominees should be Indigenous Peoples representatives from developing States where the GCF may fund activities and should be able to demonstrate relevant experience and contributions, particularly in relation to Indigenous Peoples issues, climate action, or related fields. IPAG members serve on a voluntary, non-remunerated basis, but the role involves ongoing participation, including monthly online meetings and two in-person meetings each year. Travel-related arrangements for required in-person participation may be supported in accordance with applicable GCF policies and procedures. Organizations intending to nominate a representative should begin the process early, carefully review the IPAG Terms of Reference, prepare the required organizational and nominee information, develop a clear statement addressing the membership criteria, and consider obtaining additional regional endorsements. The deadline for nominations is 9 October 2026 , and submissions should be sent to IPAGnomination@gcfund.org . For the official announcement and supporting documents, visit the Green Climate Fund s official call for nominations . Discover more global Fellowship and Climate Action opportunities on OFY. title: Disney Associate Product Manager Program 2027: Early-Career Product Management Job in the USA With Up to $130,700 Salary
summary: Are you an upcoming or recent graduate with a background in computer science, engineering, technology or another related technical field and an interest in product management? The Disney Associate Product Manager Program 2027 offers an opportunity to begin a career in product management within Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product Technology , one of the technology organisations responsible for developing and supporting products and platforms across Disney s global media business. The programme is structured as a two-year career accelerator designed to develop early-career product management talent through practical experience, formal training, mentorship, networking and exposure to different product teams. Full-time hires for the programme will begin as a cohort in Summer 2027 . Participants will also complete a team rotation at the 12-month mark, giving them exposure to multiple teams and product domains. The position is currently listed for Glendale, California, and New York, New York , with the primary location identified as the Greater Los Angeles area. The final location and team placement will depend on business needs and team alignment at the time an offer is made. The role was posted by Disney on September 15, 2026 , under Job ID 10160554 . About the Disney Associate Product Manager Program The Associate Product Manager, or APM, Program is intended to provide a structured entry point into product management for talented early-career professionals. Rather than simply placing a new graduate into an entry-level position without structured development, Disney describes the programme as a two-year career accelerator . The programme combines: Full-time employment. Hands-on product development experience. Structured product management training. Mentorship from Disney product leaders. Cross-functional collaboration. Data and user research. Strategic problem-solving. Leadership development. Professional networking. Exposure to multiple product teams through a rotation. New hires will join the programme as a cohort in Summer 2027 . After the first 12 months, participants will rotate to another team, allowing them to experience different product domains and broaden their understanding of product management. This structure is particularly relevant to graduates who want to develop a career that combines technology, business strategy, user experience, data analysis and product development. About Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product Technology The Associate Product Manager Program sits within Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product Technology . This is a global organisation made up of professionals working across areas such as: Engineering. Product development. Design. Technology. Data science. Product management. Digital platforms. Media technology. The organisation s work supports Disney s media businesses and its portfolio of brands and platforms. According to the job description, teams collaborate across brands including: Disney+ Hulu ESPN ABC ABC News National Geographic Marvel Star Wars The broader purpose is to combine technology and creativity to build products, improve consumer experiences and develop the technological infrastructure supporting Disney s media business around the world. For an aspiring product manager, this means the programme offers exposure to an environment where technology and entertainment intersect. What Makes the Disney APM Program Different? The role is designed around development rather than simply assigning graduates routine tasks. The programme gives participants an opportunity to learn how products are conceived, developed, launched and improved. Disney highlights three broad aspects of its technology and product environment: Building the Future of Media Disney s technology teams work on platforms that support media, advertising and distribution. This means product professionals can work on technology that contributes to how audiences discover, access and interact with content. Reach, Scale and Impact The products developed by Disney s technology organisation support interactions with millions of consumers around the world. For an APM, this provides the possibility of learning how product decisions operate at significant scale. Innovation Disney s technology teams work on new products and platforms and address complex technical and business challenges. The APM programme therefore provides exposure to product development in a large global media and entertainment organisation. Two-Year Career Accelerator Structure One of the central features of the opportunity is its two-year structure. Year One: Building Product Management Foundations During the initial stage, participants will develop practical experience working with product teams. They can expect exposure to areas such as: Product discovery. Product requirements. User stories. Market research. Data analysis. Product strategy. Roadmap development. Feature development. Launch planning. Cross-functional collaboration. The programme also provides structured training and mentorship. Year Two: Team Rotation and Broader Product Exposure At the 12-month mark , participants will rotate teams. The purpose of the rotation is to provide exposure to multiple teams and product domains. This can help participants develop a broader understanding of: Different types of products. Different customer or user needs. Different technical environments. Different business objectives. Different product development approaches. Cross-functional team structures. The rotation is an important part of the programme because product management can vary considerably depending on the product, customers, technology and business model. What Will an Associate Product Manager Do? The role is formally positioned as Product Manager I (APM) . The successful candidate will assist with the development and execution of product strategies designed to support business objectives. The role involves working throughout the product lifecycle, from discovery and research through development and launch. The position provides opportunities to learn from experienced product professionals while contributing to projects within The Walt Disney Company. Key Responsibilities The APM will work across several aspects of product management. 1. Collaborate With Product, Design and Engineering Teams The APM will work with: Product Managers. Designers. Engineers. Other cross-functional stakeholders. The objective is to help develop features within an assigned product domain. This requires the ability to communicate effectively with people who have different professional backgrounds and responsibilities. 2. Develop Product Strategy Participants will learn how to develop and communicate a strategic vision. This includes thinking about: User needs. Business objectives. Market trends. Product opportunities. Fan engagement. Product improvements. The role therefore goes beyond simply managing a list of technical tasks. 3. Write Product Requirements The APM will write detailed product documentation. This can include: Product requirements. User stories. Feature documentation. Strategy documents. Other materials used to guide development. Strong writing and communication skills are therefore important. 4. Work on OKRs and Product Roadmaps The APM will work with leadership on: Product strategy. Objectives and Key Results. Product roadmaps. This introduces participants to the strategic planning side of product management. 5. Conduct Market and Competitor Research Product managers need to understand the environment in which their products operate. The APM will support product research by analysing competitor offerings. This can help the product team understand: What competing products offer. How user experiences compare. Where opportunities for improvement exist. How market trends may affect product decisions. 6. Analyse Data The role includes basic data analysis to inform product decisions. Examples include analysing: Usage metrics. User behaviour. Product performance. Other relevant data. The objective is to use evidence to understand problems and support product decisions. 7. Support Product Launches The APM will contribute to feature launches and internal communications. This provides experience with the transition from product development to implementation and release. Skills Disney Is Looking For The job posting identifies several basic qualifications. Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills Applicants should have strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities. The ability to use data-driven insights to inform decisions and measure performance is particularly important. A strong candidate should therefore be comfortable asking: What problem are we solving? What does the available data tell us? How are users behaving? What should we improve? How can we measure whether an improvement worked? Communication Skills Excellent written and verbal communication skills are required. Product managers frequently serve as a bridge between technical and non-technical stakeholders. They need to communicate: Product requirements. Strategy. User needs. Business objectives. Product decisions. Roadmaps. Priorities. Product or Technical Experience Disney does not require applicants to have already worked as professional product managers. The posting accepts experience gained through: Coursework. Academic projects. Internships. Relevant areas include: Product management. Engineering. Software development. User experience. This makes the programme particularly relevant to students and recent graduates who have developed practical experience through university or internships. Understanding User Value Applicants should be able to recognise what makes a product valuable to users. Product management is fundamentally concerned with creating products that solve meaningful problems for users while also meeting organisational objectives. Candidates should therefore demonstrate an interest in: User needs. User experience. Product quality. Product improvement. Business outcomes. Interest in Technology and Product Development The role requires an interest in: Product development. User experience. Technology. Applicants do not necessarily need to be software engineers, but they should be comfortable working in a technology-driven environment. Adaptability The Disney environment is described as dynamic and fast-paced. Candidates should be capable of learning quickly and adapting when priorities change. This is particularly relevant to product management because product priorities can change based on: User feedback. Data. Business priorities. Market conditions. Technical constraints. Competitor activity. Collaboration Product management is highly collaborative. The successful candidate will work across different functions and must be able to build strong professional relationships. Disney therefore seeks applicants with a collaborative mindset and the ability to work effectively in team-oriented environments. Educational Requirements The required education is: An upcoming or recent graduate with a Bachelor s or Master s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related technical field. Relevant related fields may include disciplines closely connected to technology, software, engineering or other technical product-development areas. Applicants should carefully assess whether their academic programme falls within the related technical field requirement. The vacancy does not state that applicants must have a specific number of years of professional experience. Instead, it specifically accommodates upcoming and recent graduates , with relevant experience potentially coming from coursework, projects and internships. Learn More HERE Who Should Consider Applying? The programme may be relevant to students and recent graduates who want to build careers in: Product management. Technology. Digital products. Software. User experience. Product strategy. Data-informed decision-making. Technology-enabled media. Consumer technology. Digital entertainment. A candidate might come from a computer science programme, engineering programme or another technical discipline and have developed product-management interests through an internship, university project, student organisation or independent product project. Salary and Compensation The listed hiring range for the position in Los Angeles is: US$97,500 to US$130,700 per year. The actual base salary offered can vary based on factors including: Internal equity. Geographic region. Job-related knowledge. Skills. Experience. Other relevant considerations. Disney also states that a bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be provided as part of the compensation package. Additional medical, financial and other benefits may also apply depending on the level and position offered. Applicants should therefore distinguish between the advertised salary range and the compensation package ultimately offered to an individual candidate. Location of the Associate Product Manager Program The job is listed for: Glendale, California, United States and New York, New York, United States. The posting identifies the Greater Los Angeles, California area as the primary location , while additional opportunities may be available in New York. Final location and team placement will be determined at the time of the offer according to business needs and team alignment. Candidates should therefore be open to the locations listed in the vacancy. Start Date Full-time new hires for the programme will start as a cohort in: Summer 2027 This means the opportunity is intended for candidates preparing to transition from university into a full-time professional product-management career. Is There an Application Deadline? The supplied Disney vacancy does not state a specific application closing date . The position was posted on September 15, 2026 , and applicants should therefore check the official Disney Careers listing regularly because job postings can change or close when recruitment needs are met. Candidates interested in the programme should not assume that the position will remain open until a particular future date. Disney s Approach to Diversity and Inclusion Disney states that Disney Entertainment Sports LLC is an equal opportunity employer. According to the vacancy, applicants are considered without regard to factors including: Race. Religion. Colour. Sex. Sexual orientation. Gender identity. Gender expression. National origin. Ancestry. Age. Marital status. Military or veteran status. Medical condition. Genetic information. Disability. Other bases prohibited by applicable law. The company also states that it welcomes job seekers with disabilities and veterans with disabilities. This information describes Disney s stated employment policy; applicants should separately verify any work-authorization or immigration requirements that may apply to employment in the United States. How to Prepare for the Disney APM Application Candidates can take several practical steps before applying. 1. Build a Product-Focused Resume A technical degree alone may not demonstrate product-management potential. Applicants should highlight projects and experiences that demonstrate: Problem-solving. User research. Product thinking. Data analysis. Technical knowledge. Leadership. Communication. Teamwork. Project execution. If you have completed a university project that involved identifying a user problem and developing a technology-based solution, explain your role and the outcome clearly. 2. Highlight Relevant Internships Relevant internships can demonstrate exposure to: Product development. Software. Engineering. UX. Data. Technology. Business strategy. Applicants should explain what they actually accomplished rather than simply listing the internship title. 3. Demonstrate Data Skills The APM role involves data analysis. Candidates should therefore highlight experience with: Data interpretation. Metrics. User behaviour. Analytics. Research. Evidence-based decision-making. Where appropriate, applicants can describe specific projects in which data influenced a decision. 4. Show User-Centred Thinking Product managers need to understand users. Candidates should demonstrate that they can think about: Who the user is. What problem the user faces. Why the problem matters. What solution could address it. How success would be measured. 5. Prepare for Product Management Interviews Applicants should be prepared to discuss product-related problems and explain how they would approach them. Useful areas to practise include: Product design. Product strategy. User research. Prioritisation. Metrics. Market analysis. Competitor research. Product launches. Stakeholder management. Communication. Candidates should be prepared to explain their reasoning rather than simply provide an answer. How to Demonstrate Product Thinking A useful way to structure responses to product questions is to begin with the user and the problem. For example: Identify the target user. Define the problem. Understand why the problem matters. Identify potential solutions. Consider technical and business constraints. Prioritise possible solutions. Define success metrics. Consider how the product would be tested. Measure results. Improve the product based on evidence. This type of structured thinking aligns with the responsibilities described in the Disney APM role, including product research, user insights, strategy, roadmaps and data analysis. Understanding the Disney Product Environment One distinctive feature of the role is the scale and diversity of the company s media ecosystem. Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product Technology supports products and platforms associated with major Disney brands and media properties. The vacancy describes an environment where technology is used to: Improve storytelling. Build consumer experiences. Support media distribution. Support advertising. Develop digital platforms. Connect audiences with content. Solve complex technical challenges. For a product-management candidate, this means the work can involve the intersection of technology, business, content and consumer behaviour. Career Development and Mentorship The APM programme includes structured training and mentorship from Disney product leaders. This provides early-career professionals with access to people who have experience managing products and product teams. The development experience includes learning opportunities focused on: Product management fundamentals. Strategic problem-solving. Leadership. Networking. Product strategy. Data-informed decision-making. The two-year structure also provides time for participants to develop beyond a short-term internship experience. Product Management Skills You Can Develop Through the programme s responsibilities and training structure, participants can develop skills across several areas. Product Strategy Understanding how product objectives connect with broader business goals. Product Discovery Learning how to identify user problems and opportunities. User Research Using user insights and behaviour to understand product needs. Data Analysis Using metrics and behavioural data to inform decisions. Roadmapping Helping teams determine which features and initiatives should be developed and when. Product Requirements Writing detailed requirements and user stories that help engineering and design teams execute. Stakeholder Management Working with product, design, engineering and leadership teams. Communication Explaining product strategy and decisions clearly to different audiences. Launch Management Supporting the process of taking features from development into launch. The programme begins in Summer 2027. It is structured as a two-year career accelerator. Team rotations occur after 12 months. The primary location is Greater Los Angeles. New York may also be available. Final team and location are determined at the time of offer. title: FCDO Research Advisory Group 2026: Part-Time Remote Opportunity for Senior Global Research and Policy Experts
summary: The FCDO Research Advisory Group (RAG) is seeking experienced experts to join its advisory group and provide independent scientific and research advice to the UK Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office (FCDO) . This is a senior-level, part-time advisory opportunity for individuals with substantial expertise in areas such as health, agriculture, climate, energy, water, economic growth, humanitarian affairs, education, governance, conflict, social development, data for development, big data and artificial intelligence . Members will contribute strategic advice on FCDO s research priorities, funding portfolio, evidence use, research quality, value for money, emerging global challenges and connections with the wider UK and international research community. The position is remote, part-time and unremunerated , although FCDO will reimburse reasonable economy travel and incidental expenses associated with the role. About the FCDO Research Advisory Group The FCDO Research Advisory Group was established in 2022 to provide strategic guidance, rapid insight and independent challenge to FCDO s research funding portfolio. The Group supports the work of the FCDO Chief Scientific Adviser (CSA) , who is also the Director of the Research and Evidence Division. Its role is to help assure the quality, relevance and appropriateness of FCDO s research portfolio . The Group brings together experts with thematic and geographic knowledge covering a wide range of global development and international policy issues. Its areas of expertise include: Health Agriculture Climate Energy Water Economic growth Humanitarian affairs Education Governance Conflict Social development Data for development Big data Artificial intelligence Innovation and related research areas Members are expected to contribute their expertise while also engaging with issues that extend beyond their own individual academic discipline. What Is the Role of an FCDO Research Advisory Group Member? Members provide independent scientific and research advice to FCDO . The role is not simply about advising on an individual s specialist field. Members are appointed in a personal capacity , meaning they serve as independent experts rather than representatives of their employer, profession, institution or an interest group. Members are also expected to contribute across the Group s broader agenda. Their responsibilities include providing insight into how research and evidence can support international development and wider foreign policy objectives. Key Responsibilities 1. Advising on FCDO Research Priorities Members will contribute to discussions concerning: FCDO s research priorities Research activities The relationship between FCDO research and the wider UK science base Connections with international research communities Emerging areas where additional research may be required Their advice can help FCDO consider whether its research portfolio is addressing important global challenges and research needs. 2. Supporting Evidence-Informed Policy A central responsibility of the Group is helping ensure that FCDO policy is informed by the best available research and evidence . Members may therefore be asked to consider the quality, relevance and usefulness of research being used to inform policy. This requires an understanding of how research can be translated into practical policy and development impact. 3. Reviewing Research Programme Effectiveness Members will comment on the: Effectiveness of research programmes Value for money of research investments Funding mechanisms for research and development Performance and relevance of research activities This means applicants should be able to engage with questions concerning not only academic quality but also the practical impact and effectiveness of research funding. 4. Advising on the Research Portfolio Members will help assess the overall balance and adequacy of FCDO s research portfolio. This includes identifying: Research gaps Areas requiring greater attention Areas that may deserve less emphasis Emerging research priorities Opportunities for strengthening the overall portfolio Members therefore need to be able to think beyond individual research projects and consider research strategically at portfolio level. 5. Horizon-Scanning and Scenario Planning The Group also participates in horizon-scanning and long-range scenario planning . This involves considering emerging global challenges and developments that could have implications for research, international development and policy. Experts should therefore be comfortable thinking about future trends and possible challenges rather than focusing exclusively on current issues. 6. Connecting FCDO With Specialist Expertise Members can provide advice and connections to specialist expertise across: The UK research community International research institutions Academic networks Relevant specialist fields Global research communities Their networks and understanding of the international research environment can therefore contribute to the Group s advisory role. 7. Emergency Response and Disaster Preparedness Where required, members may also provide advice on scientific inputs to FCDO s emergency response and disaster preparedness . This responsibility highlights the importance of having experts who can apply research and evidence to rapidly changing international situations. Time Commitment The position is designed to be compatible with other professional responsibilities. Members are expected to participate in: Four meetings per year Approximately 2.5 to 3 hours per meeting Approximately 2 to 3 hours of reading and preparation for each meeting Occasional additional meetings or direct engagement when FCDO requires specific expert advice Meeting papers are expected to be circulated approximately one week before each meeting , allowing members time to review the material and prepare. Meeting dates will be confirmed as far in advance as possible. There may also be occasional ad hoc requests for expert input between scheduled meetings. Length of Appointment The appointment is for: Three years The term is renewable once , with a maximum of: Two terms This means a member may potentially serve for up to six years if their appointment is renewed. Remuneration and Expenses The position is unremunerated . Members do not receive a salary for serving on the Research Advisory Group. However, the information provided states that reasonable travel expenses and incidental expenses will be reimbursed by FCDO . Where travel is required, the stated provision is for economy travel . Applicants should therefore understand that this is a professional advisory appointment rather than a salaried part-time employment position. Employment Arrangement The position is listed as: Employment Type: Part Time Location: Remote The remote nature of the role means that members can participate without being based at a particular FCDO office. However, applicants should take into account that the role may involve meetings or activities requiring travel, with reasonable eligible travel and incidental expenses reimbursed according to the stated arrangements. Who Is FCDO Looking For? The Research Advisory Group is seeking individuals with a combination of subject-matter expertise, senior professional experience, international perspective and the ability to provide independent advice . The selection criteria emphasize several important characteristics. Selection Criteria 1. Relevant Thematic Expertise Applicants should have expertise, skills and experience in a relevant thematic area. The identified thematic areas include: Health Agriculture Climate Energy Water Growth Humanitarian affairs Education Governance Conflict Social development Data for development Applicants whose expertise relates to broader research, innovation, technology or evidence issues may also be relevant where their expertise connects with the Group s agenda. 2. Seniority and International Reputation The Group is looking for individuals with an appropriate level of seniority and international reputation . This is therefore a senior expert/advisory appointment rather than an entry-level opportunity. Applicants should be able to demonstrate a substantial record of expertise and contribution in their relevant field. 3. Familiarity With Government Processes Applicants should have familiarity with: Government processes Key government policies Policy development The relationship between research and government decision-making Experience of working with government, public institutions or policy environments can therefore be relevant to the role. 4. Independence and Fairness Members must be committed to a fair and independent process . Because the Group provides independent advice, members are expected to approach issues objectively and contribute professional judgement without allowing personal or institutional interests to determine their advice. 5. Breadth of Academic Discipline The selection process values breadth across academic disciplines. Applicants should have an understanding of transdisciplinary approaches to global challenges . This is important because many of the issues addressed by FCDO cannot be examined through one discipline alone. For example, challenges involving climate, health, development, conflict or technology can involve multiple scientific, social, economic and policy perspectives. 6. International and Global Perspective Applicants should have an international and global perspective. Particular emphasis is placed on: Capacity strengthening in the Global South Translation of research into impact Research partnerships Working with international partners Understanding how research can contribute to development outcomes Experience working across countries, regions or international research networks may therefore be relevant. FCDO Research and Development Context The Research Advisory Group operates within a broader FCDO research and development environment. Following publication of the Global Research and Technology Development (GRTD) Approach Paper , launch of the GRTD website and confirmation of long-term funding, FCDO s research and development portfolio now includes: A large Official Development Assistance (ODA) programme A smaller but growing non-ODA portfolio The non-ODA component is focused on broader foreign policy and national security objectives . This means the Group s work extends across a diverse research portfolio involving development, international policy and other strategic priorities. Appointment in a Personal Capacity A significant condition of the appointment is that members serve in their personal capacity . They are not appointed as representatives of: Their employer Their university Their profession An interest group Another organization Members are also expected to contribute across the full agenda of the Research Advisory Group , rather than restricting their contribution exclusively to their own academic discipline. This makes breadth of perspective and the ability to engage with multidisciplinary issues particularly important. Principles and Standards Expected of Members Members must abide by the Seven Principles of Public Life , commonly known as the Nolan Principles . They are also expected to take account of the Government Chief Scientific Adviser (GCSA) s Principles of Scientific Advice to Government . These expectations reinforce the importance of: Independence Integrity Evidence Professional conduct Responsible advisory practice Transparency around interests Declaration of Interests Successful members must complete a declaration of interests when appointed. The declaration must also be kept up to date throughout their appointment. This is important because members may be involved in discussions concerning research programmes, funding mechanisms and research priorities. Applicants should therefore be prepared to disclose relevant interests and maintain accurate declarations during their term. Confidentiality and Information Security Members will have responsibilities concerning FCDO information and documentation. FCDO documents and information used by the Group are Official UK Government papers and must not be shared outside the Group. Members will therefore be responsible for safeguarding: FCDO documents Research-related information Meeting papers Advisory materials Other official information provided to the Group Applicants should be comfortable working within appropriate confidentiality and information-security requirements. Selection Process The selection process involves several stages. Step 1: Submit an Application Interested applicants are required to submit: A CV An expression of interest The application should demonstrate how the applicant s experience, expertise and perspective correspond to the requirements of the Research Advisory Group. Step 2: Shortlisting Applications will be reviewed and suitable candidates will be shortlisted. The selection criteria include thematic expertise, seniority, international reputation, government familiarity, independence, multidisciplinary perspective and international experience. Step 3: Panel Interview Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a panel interview. The panel will be led by the Co-Chairs and will include the: Chief Scientific Adviser (CSA), and/or Deputy Chief Scientific Adviser (Deputy CSA) Candidates should therefore be prepared to discuss their expertise, experience, understanding of research-policy relationships and ability to contribute to the Group s broader agenda. Application Deadline The stated application deadline is: 30 September at 11:59 PM UK time Important Application Form Instruction Because this is a part-time and unremunerated position , applicants are specifically instructed to enter: N/A in both the: Salary expectations field Notice period field Applicants should follow this instruction rather than entering a salary expectation or employment notice period. How to Apply Applicants interested in joining the FCDO Research Advisory Group should prepare a strong CV and expression of interest addressing their suitability for the position. The application should demonstrate relevant evidence of: Thematic expertise Senior professional experience International experience or perspective Understanding of government and policy processes Independent and fair judgement Multidisciplinary or transdisciplinary experience Research translation and impact Capacity strengthening, particularly in the Global South Relevant professional and academic networks Ability to contribute to the Group beyond a narrow disciplinary area Applicants should also ensure that the salary expectations and notice period fields contain N/A , as instructed in the vacancy announcement. Read Full Details about this Job opportunity HERE Conclusion The Member, FCDO Research Advisory Group opportunity provides experienced research and policy experts with the opportunity to contribute independent scientific and research advice to the UK s Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office.
