title: EU Delegation Vienna Funded Traineeships 2027: Paid Opportunities for Young Graduates in International Relations, Diplomacy and Global Affairs
summary: Are you a young graduate interested in international relations, diplomacy, European affairs, international organisations, security, human rights or multilateral cooperation? The European Union Delegation to the International Organisations in Vienna is offering funded traineeships for young graduates across several sections of its diplomatic mission. These traineeships provide an opportunity to gain practical experience inside an EU Delegation and to observe how the European Union represents its interests and values within international organisations based in Vienna. The 2027 traineeship call covers several areas, including the United Nations Section, OSCE Section, Nuclear and Non-Proliferation Section, and Administrative/Head of Delegation Section . The traineeships can last for up to six months , subject to budget availability, with the earliest anticipated start in March 2027 and a possible additional intake during the second semester of 2027. The application deadline is 30 September 2026 . Successful trainees receive a monthly grant to cover living expenses , although applicants should note that travel, visa, insurance and accommodation costs are to be borne by the trainee. This opportunity is particularly relevant for graduates who want to build experience in European foreign policy, diplomacy, international organisations, multilateral affairs, international security, human rights, nuclear non-proliferation, public diplomacy or EU external action. About the EU Delegation to the International Organisations in Vienna The European Union maintains a Delegation in Vienna that works with several major international organisations headquartered or represented in the city. Vienna is an important centre for multilateral diplomacy and international cooperation. Organisations and institutions connected to the Delegation s work include bodies such as the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, United Nations Industrial Development Organization, United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs, United Nations Commission on International Trade Law, Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, International Atomic Energy Agency and other international organisations. The traineeship therefore provides exposure to an environment where international policy, diplomacy, security, development, human rights, international law and multilateral negotiations intersect. The current call was published by the European External Action Service on 15 September 2026 as a new opportunity. What the Funded Traineeship Offers The EU Delegation is offering traineeships of up to six months , subject to budget availability. The tentative starting period is the first semester of 2027 , with the earliest possible starting date being March 2027 . Depending on availability, traineeships may also begin during the second semester of 2027. Selected trainees will receive a monthly traineeship grant intended to cover living expenses . The EEAS notes that the amount may be updated before the traineeship begins, meaning applicants should not assume that a particular historical grant amount will apply to the 2027 intake. However, the financial support does not mean that every cost associated with relocating to Vienna will be covered. Applicants are responsible for: Travel costs. Visa costs where applicable. Insurance costs. Accommodation costs. Other expenses that are not covered by the traineeship grant. Candidates should therefore consider the full cost of living in Vienna and their personal financial circumstances before accepting a traineeship. Traineeship Sections Available The 2027 call covers several sections of the EU Delegation. Applicants can express interest in one traineeship per delegation , although the Delegation states that, depending on an applicant s profile, it may offer a traineeship in another section. The sections include: United Nations Section OSCE Section Nuclear and Non-Proliferation Section Administrative and Head of Delegation Section Each section offers a different type of professional experience. 1. Traineeship in the United Nations Section The UN Section supports the Head of Delegation in the role of Ambassador of the European Union towards international organisations based in Vienna. The section works across a broad multilateral agenda involving organisations and topics including: UNODC UNIDO UNOOSA UNCITRAL Drugs and crime Outer space Industrial development Multilateral cooperation EU statements and positions Outreach to international organisations Relations with third countries Public diplomacy The section also prepares reports and information for the European External Action Service and the European Commission . This makes the UN traineeship particularly relevant to graduates interested in diplomacy, international organisations, European foreign policy, multilateralism, international development, international law and global governance. Main Tasks in the UN Section Trainees may assist permanent staff with: Preparing meetings and diplomatic activities. Drafting briefings. Preparing reports. Drafting statements and other official documents. Participating in meetings. Taking notes during meetings. Supporting public diplomacy activities. These responsibilities can help trainees develop practical skills in diplomatic writing, policy analysis, meeting reporting and international relations. 2. Traineeship in the OSCE Section The OSCE Section supports the Deputy Head of Delegation in her role as EU Ambassador to the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe. The OSCE s work covers three broad dimensions of security: Politico-military security. Economic and environmental security. Human rights and fundamental freedoms. The section follows a wide range of regional and thematic issues. The current notice identifies Russia s war of aggression against Ukraine as an important part of the organisation s current agenda, alongside issues such as: Trafficking in human beings. Transnational threats. Economic and environmental aspects of security. Human rights. Fundamental freedoms. Regional political developments. The section represents the EU at OSCE meetings and events, prepares and coordinates EU statements and messages, engages with third countries and prepares reports and briefings for the EEAS and EU institutions. It also conducts public diplomacy activities highlighting EU achievements. Main Tasks in the OSCE Section A trainee may be expected to: Monitor developments across the OSCE s three security dimensions. Attend OSCE meetings with permanent staff. Support work on regional and thematic dossiers. Assist with EU coordination and outreach activities. Help draft and review EU statements and messages. Take notes during OSCE and EU meetings. Prepare reports on meetings and consultations. Conduct background research on EU and OSCE topics. Support public diplomacy activities. This section is particularly relevant to graduates interested in international security, European security policy, conflict and peace studies, human rights, international relations and multilateral diplomacy. 3. Traineeship in the Nuclear and Non-Proliferation Section The Nuclear and Non-Proliferation Section , abbreviated as NNP, deals with a specialised area of international security policy. Its work covers a dense multilateral agenda concerning nuclear issues and non-proliferation. The section follows activities involving the: International Atomic Energy Agency. Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty Organization. Nuclear safety. Nuclear security. Nuclear safeguards. Technical cooperation. Non-proliferation. Export controls. Nuclear-related international negotiations. The current notice specifically refers to issues involving Ukraine, Iran, the Democratic People s Republic of Korea and Syria, as well as nuclear safety, security and safeguards. The section also coordinates the EU s contribution to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty process. Main Tasks in the NNP Section Trainees may assist permanent staff with: Preparing meetings. Supporting diplomatic activities. Drafting briefings. Preparing reports. Drafting statements. Participating in meetings. Taking meeting notes. Supporting public diplomacy activities. This traineeship can be particularly relevant to graduates interested in international security, nuclear policy, non-proliferation, international organisations, diplomacy, international law and European foreign and security policy. 4. Administrative and Head of Delegation Section The fourth area combines work connected to the Administrative Section and the Head of Delegation Section . This opportunity is different from the specialist political traineeships because the requirements are different. For the ADMIN section, a Bachelor s degree in a relevant discipline is sufficient , while candidates also need B2 German language skills . Policy-document drafting experience is not required for this section, but numeracy is considered essential. Administrative Section The Administrative Section is responsible for essential operational processes that allow the Delegation to function effectively. Its responsibilities include areas such as: Financial management. Budget management. Procurement. Document archiving. Protocol matters. Liaison with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. VAT exemption processes. Diplomatic cards. Administrative coordination. Head of Delegation Section The Head of Delegation Section provides strategic and organisational support to the EU Ambassador. Its work includes: Internal coordination. Policy coordination across Delegation sections. High-level diplomatic visits. High-level meetings. Formal events. Social events. Official correspondence. Agenda management. Press relations. Public diplomacy. Cultural diplomacy. Digital communication. Website management. Social media. Public events and campaigns. Team Europe coordination. Administrative and financial tasks. Main Tasks for ADMIN/HoD Trainees A trainee may assist with: General administrative and office tasks. Protocol activities. Updating internal guides. Updating contact lists. Maintaining distribution lists. Meeting and visit logistics. Representation activities. Social events. Creating social media content. Updating the Delegation website. Payment files. Archiving. Ad hoc administrative requests. This section may therefore be particularly useful for graduates interested in diplomacy, administration, communications, protocol, public diplomacy, event management and international institutional operations. Before applying, you are requested to examine the dedicated website as well as the general eligibility criteria for a paid traineeship (Article 8 of the Decision ADMIN(2017)28 – Paid traineeship). Source: https://www.eeas.europa.eu/delegations/vienna-international-organisations/funded-traineeships-young-graduates-eu-delegation-international-organisations-vienna-multiple_en?s=66 Who Is Eligible to Apply? The eligibility requirements differ slightly depending on the section. For the UN, OSCE and Nuclear and Non-Proliferation sections, the Vienna call specifies that applicants must hold a Master s degree in a relevant discipline . Candidates without a Master s degree are explicitly stated to be ineligible for these traineeships. Relevant academic backgrounds include: International Politics. European Studies. International Relations. International Law. International Economics. Related disciplines connected to international affairs. For the ADMIN section, a relevant Bachelor s degree is sufficient. Academic Requirements by Section Section Minimum qualification UN Relevant Master s degree OSCE Relevant Master s degree Nuclear and Non-Proliferation Relevant Master s degree ADMIN/HoD Relevant Bachelor s degree Applicants should therefore select their preferred section carefully and verify that they meet the specific academic requirement. Professional Experience Requirement Candidates must have less than one year of professional experience after graduation by the time the traineeship agreement is signed . This makes the opportunity particularly suitable for recent graduates who have completed their studies and are beginning their professional careers. The EEAS general framework similarly establishes a maximum of one year of professional experience after graduation for the funded young-graduate traineeship pillar. Applicants should therefore calculate their post-graduation professional experience carefully rather than assuming that being a recent graduate automatically makes them eligible. Previous Experience in EU Institutions Applicants must not have more than six weeks of previous experience in EU Institutions . This restriction applies to previous training or employment in EU institutions and is part of the broader EEAS traineeship framework. Candidates who have already accumulated more than the permitted period should review the rules carefully before submitting an application. Language Requirements Excellent English-language skills are required for the specialist sections. The call specifically highlights English proficiency because trainees will be working in an international diplomatic environment involving meetings, policy documents, reports, statements and international organisations. Additional language abilities can strengthen a candidate s profile. The Vienna notice indicates that experience working in other OSCE languages and the ability to work in other UN languages would be an asset. For the ADMIN section , B2-level German is specifically required. Therefore, language expectations can be summarised as follows: UN: Excellent English; additional relevant languages are an asset. OSCE: Excellent English; OSCE-language skills are an asset. NNP: Excellent English; additional international working languages can be beneficial. ADMIN: B2 German is required. Additional Skills and Experience That Can Strengthen an Application The Vienna Delegation is looking for candidates with demonstrated interest in the EU s external action and international relations. For the specialist sections, relevant areas include: Security. Human rights. International organisations. The United Nations. European foreign policy. International diplomacy. Multilateral affairs. Applicants should also have experience in: Drafting policy documents. Taking meeting notes. Drafting meeting reports. Conducting background research. Preparing written briefings. Previous experience with an international organisation or diplomatic mission is considered an asset, although the notice does not state that this experience is mandatory for every applicant. What Are the Benefits of the Traineeship? The opportunity provides several forms of professional and educational value. 1. Monthly Financial Grant Selected trainees receive a monthly grant to cover living expenses . The EEAS notes that the grant information may be updated before the traineeship begins. Applicants should therefore consult the latest official financial information when preparing for the traineeship. 2. Practical Diplomatic Experience The traineeship provides exposure to the daily work of an EU diplomatic mission. Depending on the selected section, trainees can gain experience with: Diplomatic meetings. International organisations. Policy research. Briefing preparation. EU statements. Reporting. Public diplomacy. International security. Administrative operations. Communications. 3. Exposure to International Organisations Vienna is an important centre for multilateral diplomacy. Trainees in the UN, OSCE and NNP sections can gain practical exposure to the work of international organisations and the processes through which governments and international institutions address global issues. 4. Professional Writing Experience Several traineeship tasks involve producing professional documents. These can include: Briefing notes. Reports. Statements. Meeting records. Research summaries. Other diplomatic documents. This can help graduates strengthen their policy-writing and analytical skills. 5. Networking and Professional Exposure Working inside an EU Delegation can expose trainees to diplomats, EU officials, international organisations, government representatives and professionals working on international policy. This can help trainees understand the professional environment of international affairs. 6. Public Diplomacy Experience Several sections engage in public diplomacy. Trainees may support: Public events. Communications activities. Social media. Website updates. Campaigns. Visibility activities. This is particularly relevant to applicants interested in strategic communication and international public diplomacy. What Costs Does the Trainee Need to Cover? Although the opportunity is funded through a monthly grant, the financial arrangement does not mean that all expenses are covered. The official notice states that travel, visa, insurance and accommodation costs must be borne by the trainee . Applicants should therefore prepare a realistic budget that considers: Accommodation in Vienna. Transportation. Food and daily living expenses. Visa costs where applicable. Insurance. Travel to and from Vienna. Personal expenses. The monthly grant is intended to contribute toward living expenses, but applicants should not assume it will automatically cover every cost. How to Apply for the EU Delegation Vienna Traineeship Applications must be submitted by email. The designated email address is: Delegation-Vienna-Trainees@eeas.europa.eu Applicants must provide three key documents. 1. Europass Curriculum Vitae The Delegation requires a detailed standard Europass CV . Importantly, the notice states that CVs in other formats will not be considered. Applicants should therefore use the official Europass format rather than sending a conventional personal résumé: https://europa.eu/europass/en 2. Cover Letter Applicants must submit a cover letter explaining why they want to participate in an EU traineeship. The cover letter should be specific to the opportunity. Candidates should explain: Why they are interested in the EU. Why they are interested in international relations. Why they selected the relevant section. What academic experience they bring. What relevant professional or research experience they have. How their skills relate to the traineeship. What they hope to learn. 3. Application Form Applicants must also complete the official application form provided with the vacancy notice. The current application form is titled: Austria UN OSCE Vienna Application form for multiple funded traineeships 2027 Candidates should download and complete the correct form before submitting their application. Important Email Subject Requirement Applicants must use the required email subject line. The subject should follow the format: Funded Traineeship – Your Name/Acronym of the Section This requirement is important because the Delegation states that applications without the specified subject line will not be considered . Candidates should therefore avoid using generic subject lines such as: Traineeship Application Application EU Internship Vienna Internship Instead, they should follow the format requested by the Delegation. One Application Per Delegation Candidates may apply for only one traineeship per Delegation . However, the Delegation states that based on an applicant s profile, it could offer the candidate a traineeship in another section. Applicants should therefore select the section that best matches their: Academic qualifications. Professional interests. Language skills. Research experience. Career objectives. Previous international affairs experience. Application Deadline The deadline for the EU Delegation to the International Organisations in Vienna funded traineeships is: 30 September 2026 The opportunity is listed by the EEAS as a Trainee position in Vienna. Because applications must be submitted by email, candidates should avoid waiting until the final day. Preparing the Europass CV, cover letter and application form in advance can reduce the risk of submitting an incomplete application. Selection Process The Delegation will evaluate the applications after the deadline. According to the official notice: Applications are evaluated. Shortlisted candidates are contacted. Shortlisted candidates are invited for an interview. Successful candidates must provide the required documentation. Candidates who cannot provide required documentation may have their application rejected. Unsuccessful candidates are notified by email. Candidates should therefore monitor the email address used in their application after submission. Nationality and Geographic Eligibility The EEAS general framework states that funded traineeships in EU Delegations can be open to: Citizens of EU Member States. Citizens of EU candidate countries that have signed an accession agreement with the EU. Citizens of the host country, depending on the relevant traineeship pillar and applicable rules. The specific Vienna notice additionally contains requirements concerning documentation for citizens of EU Member States , including proof of appropriate coverage and relevant visa or temporary residence documentation where applicable. Because nationality rules can depend on the specific traineeship framework and host-country legislation, candidates should verify their individual eligibility against the latest EEAS rules before applying. The opportunity should therefore not be assumed to be open to applicants from every country worldwide. Requirements for EU Citizens The Vienna notice states that citizens of EU Member States must: Provide proof of coverage against the risk of a pandemic and repatriation costs. Hold a relevant entrance visa and/or temporary residence permit where applicable. Ensure that these documents comply with the traineeship agreement and local legislation. These requirements should be reviewed carefully by selected candidates before the traineeship begins. Compliance With Local and National Legislation The traineeships can only be offered in compliance with: Austrian legislation. Applicable EU rules. The legislation of the trainee s country of origin. Relevant visa and residence requirements. The terms of the traineeship agreement. Applicants should therefore understand that meeting the academic and professional requirements alone does not necessarily resolve immigration or legal requirements. How to Prepare a Strong Application Although selection is competitive, applicants can improve the clarity and relevance of their application by carefully matching their profile to the selected section. Highlight: Academic qualifications. Policy research. International relations experience. Diplomatic or international organisation exposure. Writing experience. Research skills. Step 3: Make the Cover Letter Specific Avoid sending a generic cover letter that could be used for any internship. Explain why you are interested in: The EU Delegation. Vienna. The specific section. Candidates should therefore demonstrate their ability to communicate complex information clearly and professionally. Step 5: Show Relevant Research Experience The OSCE section, for example, requires background research on EU and OSCE-related issues. Applicants should demonstrate that they can: Locate reliable information. Analyse policy developments. Summarise complex issues. Identify relevant developments. Produce concise written outputs. Step 6: Check the Email Subject This is particularly important because the notice explicitly states that applications without the required subject line will not be considered. Step 7: Submit the Complete Application Before sending the email, verify that it contains: Europass CV. Cover letter. Completed application form. Correct subject line. title: Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027: Up to £70,000 for Experienced Researchers in Any Discipline
summary: The Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027 provide funding for experienced researchers who need dedicated time to complete a programme of original research. The scheme is particularly aimed at researchers whose routine teaching and administrative responsibilities have limited their ability to undertake research in recent years. The fellowship offers up to £70,000 and can support research periods lasting between 3 and 24 months . Researchers from a wide range of academic disciplines can apply, making this an opportunity for established scholars seeking protected time to develop and complete substantial research projects. About the Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships The Research Fellowships are offered by the Leverhulme Trust , a UK charitable organisation that supports research and education. The fellowship is designed around a specific challenge faced by many experienced academics: although they may have strong research ideas and established research records, their ability to conduct research can be restricted by teaching, administration and other routine institutional responsibilities. The programme therefore provides financial support that can enable successful applicants to devote a significant period of time to their research. The Trust gives particular priority to applicants whose teaching and administrative duties have significantly affected their capacity to conduct research during the three years before applying . This makes the fellowship especially relevant to experienced researchers who can demonstrate that institutional responsibilities have prevented them from giving sufficient attention to an important original research programme. Fellowship Value Successful applicants can receive funding of up to: £70,000 The maximum value gives researchers substantial flexibility to structure an appropriate period of research leave and cover eligible costs associated with undertaking the proposed research. Applicants should nevertheless ensure that their requested budget is appropriate to the scale and requirements of their proposed project rather than simply requesting the maximum amount available. Duration of the Fellowship Research Fellowships can be held for: A minimum of 3 months Up to a maximum of 24 months The duration should correspond to the amount of dedicated research time genuinely required to complete the proposed programme. A project requiring a shorter period of concentrated research may therefore be proposed for a shorter fellowship, while a more substantial programme may require a longer period, subject to the scheme s conditions and assessment. Who Is the Fellowship Designed For? The Research Fellowships are intended for experienced researchers who want to complete a defined piece or programme of original research. The scheme is particularly relevant to researchers who: Have an established research background. Have developed an original research project that requires dedicated time to complete. Have been unable to devote sufficient time to research because of routine academic responsibilities. Have significant teaching commitments. Have substantial administrative responsibilities within their institution. Can demonstrate that these responsibilities have affected their research activity during the three years preceding the application. Are able to undertake the proposed research within the fellowship period. The Trust s emphasis on the impact of teaching and administration means that applicants should clearly explain how their professional responsibilities have constrained their research time and why the fellowship would make a meaningful difference. Research in Any Discipline One of the notable features of the Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowship is its broad disciplinary scope. The opportunity is available to researchers working across disciplines rather than being restricted to a single academic field. Depending on the nature of the proposed project, this can include research areas within fields such as: Humanities Social sciences Arts and related disciplines Natural sciences Other eligible academic research fields The breadth of the scheme means that the quality and originality of the proposed research, together with the applicant s experience and eligibility, are important considerations. Applicants should consult the official scheme guidance carefully to determine whether their particular discipline and research proposal satisfy the Trust s requirements. Why the Fellowship Is Important for Experienced Researchers Academic researchers often have responsibilities extending well beyond conducting research. Teaching, student supervision, administration, committee responsibilities, institutional projects and other duties can substantially reduce the amount of time available for original research. The Leverhulme Research Fellowship is structured to address this problem by providing support for a period in which an experienced researcher can concentrate on a specific research programme. For an applicant, the fellowship may therefore provide an opportunity to: Create dedicated research time The fellowship can help an experienced researcher obtain a sustained period away from routine responsibilities so that they can concentrate on their research. Complete an existing research programme Researchers who have already developed a substantial body of work but have struggled to bring it to completion may use the fellowship period to make significant progress. Develop original research The scheme is intended for original research, making the research question, methodology and anticipated contribution important elements of an application. Advance an established research career A successful fellowship can provide researchers with additional time and resources to develop significant scholarly work. Address research interruptions caused by academic duties Researchers whose teaching and administrative workload has reduced their research capacity can explain this context as part of their application. Priority for Researchers Affected by Teaching and Administrative Duties A particularly important feature of this fellowship is the Trust s stated priority for applicants whose research has been affected by routine institutional responsibilities. The Trust specifically indicates that priority will be given to applicants whose teaching and administrative duties have significantly impacted their ability to undertake research during the three years before the application . This means applicants should pay close attention to explaining their circumstances. Rather than simply stating that they are busy, applicants should demonstrate the relationship between their professional workload and their reduced research activity. For example, an applicant may need to explain: The nature of their teaching responsibilities. The extent of their administrative workload. How these responsibilities have affected their available research time. The period over which the impact occurred. How dedicated fellowship time would allow them to complete the proposed research. The purpose should be to establish a clear connection between the applicant s current circumstances and the need for the fellowship. What Type of Research Can Be Proposed? The fellowship is intended to support a piece or programme of original research . Consequently, applicants should have a clearly defined research objective rather than presenting a general desire to undertake academic work. A strong proposal should communicate: The central research question or problem. The significance of the research. The originality of the proposed work. The approach or methodology to be used. The work that will be undertaken during the fellowship. The expected scholarly contribution. Why the proposed fellowship period is necessary. How the research will progress during the requested period. The research programme should also be realistically structured around the amount of time and funding requested. Internationally Focused Projects The fellowship information also contains guidance concerning projects with an international focus . Researchers whose proposed work involves international subjects, locations, sources, collaborations or comparative research should carefully review the Trust s specific guidance on projects with an international focus before submitting an application. This is particularly important for researchers whose projects extend beyond the UK or involve research activities in multiple countries. Applicants should make sure that the international dimension of their proposal is clearly justified by the research itself and that all relevant eligibility and funding conditions are satisfied. Application Preparation The Leverhulme Trust advises prospective applicants to read the available information before beginning the application. The Trust has provided Application Help Notes 2027 to assist researchers in preparing their submissions. The guidance should be reviewed carefully because it contains information about the requirements and information applicants need to prepare. Applicants should ideally begin preparation well before the closing date, allowing enough time to develop their research proposal, assemble supporting information and review their application before submission. How to Apply Applications are submitted through the Leverhulme Grant System . Prospective applicants should: Review the Research Fellowships information provided by the Leverhulme Trust. Read the Application Help Notes 2027 . Develop a clearly defined original research programme. Confirm that they meet the fellowship s eligibility requirements. Consider the appropriate duration of the proposed fellowship. Prepare the information and supporting material required by the application system. Prepare a realistic funding request, taking into account the maximum fellowship value. Submit the completed application through the Leverhulme Grant System before the deadline. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit, particularly where institutional approval or additional information may be required. APPLY HERE Application Deadline The deadline for the Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027 is: 5 November 2026 Applicants should ensure that their applications are submitted before the stated closing date and should check the official application system for any submission-time requirements. Funding Amount and Duration at a Glance Feature Details Fellowship Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027 Maximum value £70,000 Fellowship duration 3 to 24 months Research area Any discipline, subject to scheme eligibility Target applicants Experienced researchers Particular priority Researchers whose teaching and administrative duties have significantly affected research during the previous three years Research focus Original research Deadline 5 November 2026 Application system Leverhulme Grant System What Applicants Should Emphasise Applicants should ensure that their proposal presents a convincing and coherent explanation of the research they intend to undertake. Several areas deserve particular attention. 1. Explain the originality of the research The application should make clear what is new about the proposed research and what contribution it is expected to make. 2. Demonstrate research experience Because the fellowship is intended for experienced researchers, applicants should present their relevant research background and demonstrate their ability to undertake the proposed work. 3. Explain the need for dedicated research time Applicants should clearly explain why the research cannot easily be completed alongside their existing teaching and administrative responsibilities. 4. Address the three-year context Researchers who have been significantly affected by teaching and administrative responsibilities should clearly explain how those duties have constrained their research activities during the relevant three-year period. 5. Develop a realistic timetable The proposed research should be achievable within the requested fellowship period. Applicants should demonstrate how the available research time will be used. 6. Prepare an appropriate budget Although the maximum award is £70,000, applicants should request an amount that is justified by the needs of their specific research programme. Research Fellowship Application Strategy A prospective applicant can strengthen the preparation process by treating the application as a coherent research case rather than simply a request for funding. The application should connect four central elements: Research problem → Original contribution → Need for dedicated time → Achievable research programme The research problem establishes what the applicant wants to investigate. The originality explains why the research matters academically. The explanation of the applicant s workload establishes why dedicated fellowship time is necessary. Finally, the research plan demonstrates that the proposed work can realistically be completed during the fellowship. This structure can help ensure that the application remains focused and that the need for fellowship support is clearly communicated. Who Can Apply? The opportunity is designed for experienced researchers . The information provided by the Leverhulme Trust does not describe the fellowship as a general scholarship for undergraduate or newly enrolled students. Applicants should therefore assess their level of research experience and their ability to demonstrate a substantive programme of original research. The Trust s emphasis on applicants affected by teaching and administrative responsibilities also means that the fellowship is particularly relevant to established researchers working within academic or research institutions. Who Is Not the Main Target of the Fellowship? Based on the stated purpose of the scheme, this opportunity is not primarily presented as a general funding programme for: Undergraduate students. Students seeking tuition funding. Applicants without an established research background. Individuals seeking general professional development funding. Projects that are not based on original research. The fellowship is specifically framed around experienced researchers seeking time to complete a programme of original research. Official Application Resources Prospective applicants should review the Leverhulme Trust s official Research Fellowships information and the Application Help Notes 2027 before preparing their application. The application is made through the Leverhulme Grant System . The Trust also provides a dedicated contact for Research Fellowship enquiries, which applicants can use if their questions are not answered in the published guidance. Conclusion The Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027 offer experienced researchers an opportunity to obtain dedicated time and financial support to complete original research. With funding of up to £70,000 and fellowship periods ranging from 3 to 24 months , the scheme can provide substantial support for researchers whose teaching and administrative responsibilities have limited their ability to pursue research. The fellowship is particularly relevant to applicants who can demonstrate that their routine academic duties have significantly affected their research capacity during the previous three years. Researchers should therefore carefully explain their research experience, the originality and importance of their proposed project, the effect of their existing responsibilities, and why a dedicated fellowship period is necessary. Interested researchers should begin preparing early, read the 2027 application guidance carefully and submit their applications through the Leverhulme Grant System before the 5 November 2026 deadline. title: EBRD Internship 2026 in Brussels: Apply for a 6-Month Intern Position in Corporate Strategy
summary: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is inviting applications for an Intern position based in Brussels, Belgium , offering an opportunity for qualified graduates and early-career professionals to gain practical experience within an international financial institution. The six-month internship is situated within the Corporate Strategy Division and will involve work related to European Union policies and initiatives, institutional communications, policy engagement, events, meetings, research, and coordination. This EBRD internship provides an opportunity for an individual with an academic degree and some professional working experience to contribute to the work of the Bank s EU Representative Office while developing professional experience in an international and multicultural environment. The position may be particularly relevant to candidates interested in European Union affairs, international development, public policy, international organisations, communications, sustainability, finance, and institutional relations . Overview of the EBRD Internship Opportunity The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is recruiting an Intern to support its team in Brussels. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of the Principal Manager and contribute to a range of policy, communication, event, meeting, administrative, and coordination activities. According to the vacancy announcement, the internship has a duration of six months and is based in Brussels, Belgium. Key Opportunity Details Organisation: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) Position: Intern Division: Corporate Strategy Location: Brussels, Belgium Office Country: Belgium Office City: Brussels Contract Type: Internship Contract Length: 6 months Requisition ID: 37050 Posting Date: 11 September 2026 Application Deadline: 25 September 2026 The vacancy is designed for an individual who can support the Brussels-based team across policy engagement, communications, events, meetings, outreach, and coordination activities. About the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is an international financial institution that works across regions in which it invests. The organisation describes its approach as agile and innovative and highlights the opportunity for employees to work with experts from a wide range of professional sectors. Working at the EBRD can expose interns and other employees to professionals operating across areas including finance, public policy, international development, government, the private sector, and institutional relations. The organisation also places emphasis on values including: Inclusiveness Innovation Trust Responsibility These values are reflected in workplace behaviours that include listening and speaking up, collaborating, acting decisively, and simplifying processes to increase impact. For an intern interested in international organisations and development-related work, the environment can provide exposure to how an international financial institution interacts with policymakers, institutions, stakeholders, and other organisations. Purpose of the EBRD Brussels Internship The primary purpose of the position is to provide support to the Brussels team across several areas of work. The intern will work under the supervision of the Principal Manager and assist with activities connected to EU policies and initiatives, communications, policy engagement, outreach, events, meetings, administration, and project coordination . Because the role combines policy and communication responsibilities, applicants may benefit from having an interest in both the institutional and public-facing aspects of international development work. The position can therefore provide practical exposure to how policy developments are monitored, analysed, communicated, and incorporated into institutional engagement. Key Responsibilities of the EBRD Intern The selected candidate will be expected to support the team in several areas. 1. Supporting Analysis of EU Policies and Initiatives One of the key responsibilities will involve supporting the analysis of and engagement with European Union policies and initiatives . This means the intern will contribute to the team s understanding of relevant EU developments and help support engagement around policies and initiatives that may be relevant to the EBRD s work. This responsibility could provide valuable exposure to EU policymaking and the relationship between international financial institutions and European institutions. 2. Supporting Communication Activities The intern will also support internal and external communication activities aimed at raising the profile of the EBRD and its EU Representative Office. Communication responsibilities may involve helping the team communicate its activities, priorities, engagements, and work to relevant audiences. This part of the position may be particularly relevant to graduates and early-career professionals with an interest in corporate communications, public affairs, institutional communications, digital communication, or international development communication. 3. Attending Relevant Events The intern will have the opportunity to attend relevant events and report back to management. This responsibility can provide exposure to professional events involving policymakers, institutions, development organisations, financial-sector stakeholders, and other relevant actors. The ability to observe discussions, identify important developments, and communicate key information clearly will therefore be useful in this role. 4. Participating in Meetings The intern may participate in internal and external meetings where appropriate. This provides an opportunity to observe and contribute to professional discussions and gain insight into how an international organisation coordinates its work and engages with external stakeholders. 5. Supporting Policy Engagement and Communication Outreach Another important component of the internship involves supporting the team with both policy engagement and communication outreach . This combines two closely connected areas: understanding and engaging with policy developments while also helping communicate the organisation s work and priorities. Candidates who are comfortable researching information, preparing written materials, communicating professionally, and working with different stakeholders may find these responsibilities particularly relevant. 6. Administrative and Coordination Support The intern will also provide occasional administrative and coordination support for other project activities. Although these tasks may be secondary to the policy and communication responsibilities, they can be important for ensuring that projects and team activities are organised effectively. Strong organisational skills, attention to detail, reliability, and the ability to manage changing priorities can therefore be valuable. Academic and Professional Qualifications The EBRD states that applicants should have a degree with some professional working experience . The vacancy does not specify a single academic discipline in the information provided. Consequently, candidates from different educational backgrounds may potentially be relevant, particularly where their studies and experience align with the responsibilities of the role. Relevant academic or professional interests may include areas such as: European studies International relations International development Public policy Political science Economics Finance Communications Corporate communications Public affairs Development studies Business International organisations Applicants should carefully review the official vacancy requirements before applying to determine whether their specific academic and professional background meets the employer s criteria. Professional Experience The vacancy requires candidates to have some professional working experience . The EBRD further notes that experience engaging with EU institutions or international organisations is a plus . This means previous experience in these environments can strengthen an applicant s relevance to the role, although the vacancy presents such experience as an advantage rather than as the stated core qualification. Experience gained through employment, internships, professional assignments, project work, or other relevant professional settings may help demonstrate an applicant s ability to operate in a structured organisational environment. Candidates should focus their application materials on experiences that demonstrate their ability to: Conduct research and analysis Understand policy developments Communicate professionally Work with different stakeholders Prepare or present information Support events and meetings Manage multiple tasks Coordinate activities Work independently Adapt to changing priorities Language Requirements Fluency in English is required for the position. Knowledge of French is an advantage . Because the role is located in Brussels and involves engagement connected to EU institutions and initiatives, language capabilities can be particularly useful when communicating in a multicultural and international environment. Applicants should clearly demonstrate their English-language proficiency and indicate any additional relevant language abilities in their application where appropriate. Knowledge of EU Institutions and Development Policy The EBRD is looking for candidates with knowledge of EU institutions and an understanding of development policy . This requirement is particularly relevant because a substantial part of the internship involves supporting the team s engagement with EU policies and initiatives. Applicants should therefore be familiar with the role and functions of relevant EU institutions and have an understanding of broader development-policy issues. A strong application should demonstrate genuine interest in the policy environment in which the EBRD operates rather than simply listing academic qualifications. Ability to Work Independently The successful candidate should be able to work independently while also understanding when it is appropriate to seek advice. This is an important professional skill in an international organisation where interns may be given individual assignments while also working as part of a wider team. Applicants can demonstrate this capability through examples of situations where they have: Managed assignments independently Met deadlines without constant supervision Taken initiative on projects Identified when additional guidance was needed Communicated challenges promptly Worked responsibly with confidential or important information Ability to Work in a Multicultural Environment The EBRD operates as an international organisation with employees and stakeholders from different professional, cultural, and national backgrounds. The vacancy therefore requires candidates to be able to operate effectively in a multicultural environment with changing priorities . Adaptability, cultural awareness, communication skills, collaboration, professionalism, and openness to different perspectives can all be valuable in such an environment. Applicants should consider highlighting experiences that demonstrate their ability to collaborate with people from different backgrounds and adapt when priorities change. What the EBRD Offers as a Workplace The EBRD describes its workplace as providing varied, stimulating, and engaging work. Employees can interact with experts working across the financial, political, public, and private sectors in the regions where the Bank operates. This type of professional exposure can allow interns to understand how different sectors interact in the context of international development and investment. The organisation also highlights several aspects of its working environment. International and Diverse Professional Environment The EBRD states that it embraces inclusion and celebrates diversity. Its workforce includes people with different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. According to the organisation, this diversity contributes fresh ideas, energy, and innovation to its work. For an intern, working in such an environment can provide an opportunity to develop cross-cultural communication and collaboration skills. Hybrid Workplace The EBRD describes its workplace as a hybrid environment , providing flexibility to teams and individuals. The organisation says its approach is based on trust, flexibility, and connectedness. Applicants should nevertheless review the official vacancy and any applicable employment information for the specific working arrangements associated with this internship. Sustainability and Digital Transformation The organisation states that sustainability, equality, and digital transformation are central elements of its environment. These themes are increasingly important across international development and financial institutions, making exposure to them potentially valuable for candidates building careers in related fields. Employee Wellbeing The EBRD also states that its workplace prioritises employee wellbeing and provides a comprehensive suite of competitive benefits. Specific benefits applicable to an intern should be confirmed from the official employment terms and vacancy information. Diversity and Inclusion at the EBRD Diversity is identified by the EBRD as one of its core values. The organisation states that it seeks to ensure that people are treated with respect, given equal opportunities, and able to work in an inclusive environment. The vacancy specifically encourages qualified candidates who are nationals of EBRD member countries to apply regardless of racial, ethnic, religious, or cultural background, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, socioeconomic background, or disability. This is an important point for prospective applicants because eligibility is linked to nationality within the EBRD member-country framework. Candidates should therefore verify that their nationality meets the EBRD s applicable eligibility requirements before submitting an application. Who Should Consider Applying? This internship may be relevant to graduates and early-career professionals who have an academic degree and some professional working experience and who are interested in areas such as: European Union affairs International development International organisations Public policy Development policy Corporate strategy Institutional relations Public affairs Strategic communications International finance Sustainability Government and stakeholder engagement Candidates who have previously engaged with EU institutions or international organisations may have particularly relevant experience because the EBRD identifies this background as an advantage. How to Prepare a Strong Application Applicants should ensure that their application clearly connects their education and professional experience to the responsibilities described in the vacancy. A strong application can demonstrate: Academic preparation – Clearly state your degree and explain how your academic background relates to the position. Professional experience – Highlight relevant professional experience rather than simply listing previous positions. EU knowledge – Demonstrate your understanding of EU institutions, policies, and initiatives. Development-policy awareness – Show familiarity with development-related issues and explain your interest in the field. Communication skills – Provide evidence of experience supporting internal or external communications. Research and analytical skills – Highlight assignments where you researched, analysed, summarised, or presented information. International experience – If applicable, mention experience working with international organisations, EU institutions, multinational teams, or multicultural stakeholders. Adaptability – Demonstrate that you can manage changing priorities while maintaining the quality of your work. Independent working ability – Give examples of projects or assignments that you successfully handled with limited supervision. Language skills – Clearly indicate your English proficiency and any French-language skills. Important Dates The EBRD published the vacancy on 11 September 2026 . The stated application deadline is 25 September 2026 . Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and should not wait until the final day if they already have the necessary documents prepared. Application Process Interested candidates should apply through the official EBRD careers platform and review the complete vacancy details before submitting their application. The official vacancy should be used to confirm all current requirements, application instructions, and any information concerning the recruitment process. The EBRD also notes that because it receives a high volume of applications, it is unable to provide detailed feedback to candidates who are not shortlisted for further consideration. APPLY HERE Why This Internship Can Be Relevant for an International Career An internship within an international financial institution can provide practical exposure to the relationship between policy, development, finance, communications, and institutional engagement. For someone seeking a career in international organisations, public policy, European affairs, development, communications, or related fields, the responsibilities outlined in this vacancy provide exposure to several professional functions within one role. The Brussels location is also significant because the city is a major centre for European institutional and policy activity. Working within the EBRD s EU Representative Office can therefore place the intern in an environment where EU policy engagement and international development intersect. Visit HERE to learn more about the EBRD Internship 2026 in Brussels. Conclusion The EBRD Intern position in Brussels offers a six-month opportunity for a qualified graduate or early-career professional to gain practical experience within the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development s Corporate Strategy Division. The role combines EU policy analysis and engagement, communication activities, event participation, meetings, outreach, administration, and project coordination , making it relevant to candidates interested in international development, European affairs, public policy, communications, international organisations, sustainability, and finance. Applicants should have a degree and some professional working experience , while experience engaging with EU institutions or international organisations is considered an advantage. Fluency in English is required, French is an advantage, and candidates should have knowledge of EU institutions, an understanding of development policy, the ability to work independently, and the capacity to operate effectively in a multicultural environment. The application deadline is 25 September 2026 . Eligible candidates should review the official vacancy carefully and submit their applications through the EBRD careers platform before the stated deadline.
