title: Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships 2027/28: Fully Funded UK Scholarships for Students from Developing Commonwealth Countries
summary: The Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships 2027/28 provide an opportunity for talented and motivated graduates from eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries to pursue full-time taught Master’s degrees at universities in the United Kingdom. Funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office, the scholarship programme is designed to support individuals who demonstrate academic potential, leadership capacity and a commitment to sustainable development but who may not otherwise be able to afford postgraduate study in the UK. The programme is administered by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK , commonly known as the CSC, under the framework of the Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan. It aims to develop skilled professionals, researchers, leaders and innovators who can contribute to the development of their home countries after completing their studies. For the 2027/28 academic year, applications are scheduled to open on 8 September 2026 , with the closing deadline set for 20 October 2026 at 16:00 British Summer Time (BST) . Applicants must also apply through an approved nominating agency, and those agencies may establish earlier internal deadlines. About the Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships The Commonwealth Master’s Scholarship is one of the Master’s-level programmes offered by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK. The CSC operates within the wider Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan, which promotes educational exchange, professional development, international collaboration and sustainable development across Commonwealth countries. The scholarship is supported by the UK government through the Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office . Its central purpose is to enable talented people from eligible developing Commonwealth countries to acquire advanced knowledge and practical skills that can contribute to social, economic and institutional development. The programme is particularly intended for candidates who: Have strong academic and professional potential. Come from eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries. Have a clear interest in sustainable development. Would not otherwise be able to finance postgraduate study in the UK. Intend to use their knowledge and skills to contribute to their home countries and communities. The CSC seeks to attract people from diverse backgrounds and support them in becoming future leaders, innovators and change-makers. Scholarship Purpose and Development Focus Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships are not simply designed to support individual academic advancement. They are also connected to the UK’s international development priorities. The programme seeks to build human capacity in Commonwealth countries by supporting postgraduate education in fields that can contribute to sustainable development. Scholars are expected to gain knowledge, professional networks and practical experience that can be applied after their return to their home countries. The scholarship programme combines several objectives: Developing advanced skills: Scholars gain specialist knowledge through postgraduate study at a UK university. Supporting sustainable development: Academic programmes are expected to connect with development needs and challenges. Strengthening institutions: Graduates can contribute to universities, public institutions, businesses, civil society organisations and other sectors. Encouraging international collaboration: Scholars become part of a wider Commonwealth network that supports cooperation between countries and institutions. Developing future leaders: The CSC supports individuals with the potential to create positive change in their professional fields and communities. The scholarships are offered under the CSC’s six development themes. Applicants should therefore demonstrate how their proposed Master’s programme relates to development priorities and how the knowledge gained may contribute to meaningful outcomes in their home country. More information about the development themes is available through the official CSC development themes page . What the Scholarship Supports The Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships are designed to enable successful candidates to undertake full-time taught Master’s study at a UK university. The scholarship is intended for applicants who could not otherwise afford to study in the United Kingdom. The precise financial terms, allowances and conditions should be checked in the official scholarship guidance for the relevant application year. Applicants should carefully review the official financial assistance information before applying, as the scholarship’s funding arrangements may include specific conditions relating to: Tuition fees. Living and maintenance support. Travel arrangements. Allowances and other approved expenses. Scholarship duration. University placement. Immigration and visa requirements. Return to the scholar’s home country after completion. Candidates should not assume that every cost associated with studying in the UK will automatically be covered. All financial provisions should be confirmed through the official CSC guidance and scholarship terms. Study Level and Programme Type The Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships support: Full-time taught Master’s programmes. Study at eligible universities in the United Kingdom. Postgraduate programmes that align with the CSC’s development themes. Academic programmes that can contribute to sustainable development in eligible Commonwealth countries. The scholarship is not intended to fund every type of postgraduate programme. Applicants should carefully review the official restrictions on eligible courses and confirm that their chosen programme meets the CSC’s requirements. The CSC’s frequently asked questions indicate that the programme does not fund MBAs or research-based Master’s programmes. Applicants should therefore distinguish between a taught Master’s programme and a research Master’s programme before preparing an application. Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships 2027/28 Important Dates The official application timetable for the 2027/28 academic year is as follows: Activity Date Applications open 8 September 2026 CSC application deadline 20 October 2026 at 16:00 BST Expected period of study September/October 2027 Nominating agencies submit candidates December 2026 Expected notification of results July 2027 Applicants must remember that nominating agencies may set their own deadlines, which may be earlier than the CSC’s final deadline. Therefore, candidates should not wait until 20 October 2026 before contacting their national nominating agency. An applicant who misses the agency’s internal deadline may not be considered, even if the CSC application portal remains open. Who Can Apply? The Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships are intended for candidates from eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries. To be considered, applicants must generally satisfy the following eligibility requirements. 1. Citizenship or Refugee Status Applicants must: Be a citizen of an eligible Commonwealth country; Have been granted refugee status by an eligible Commonwealth country; or Be a British Protected Person. Applicants who do not fall within one of these categories may not be eligible for this particular scholarship programme. 2. Permanent Residence Applicants must be permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country. This requirement is important because the programme is designed to support candidates who are connected to eligible Commonwealth countries and who are expected to use their knowledge and skills to contribute to development in those countries. Temporary residence, study residence or a short-term stay in an eligible country may not be sufficient. Applicants should review the official eligibility rules carefully if their citizenship and residence countries differ. 3. Academic Qualification By the relevant start date, applicants must normally hold: A first degree of at least upper second-class honours standard, commonly referred to as a 2:1; or A lower second-class degree together with a relevant postgraduate qualification, usually a Master’s degree. The exact interpretation of degree classifications may vary by country and education system. Applicants should provide accurate academic records and ensure that their qualifications meet the CSC’s minimum standard. Candidates should also confirm whether their proposed UK university requires a particular degree subject, grade, prerequisite course or professional qualification for admission. 4. Financial Need The scholarship is aimed at candidates who would not otherwise be able to afford to study in the United Kingdom. Applicants should be prepared to explain their financial circumstances and why scholarship support is necessary for them to undertake the proposed Master’s programme. Financial need is an important part of the programme’s purpose. Applicants should provide truthful, clear and consistent information about their circumstances rather than treating the scholarship as a general funding opportunity available regardless of financial need. 5. Availability to Begin Study Successful candidates must be available to begin academic studies in the UK at the start of the UK academic year in September or October 2027. Applicants should consider: Their graduation timeline. University admission requirements. Visa processing. Passport validity. Academic commitments in their home country. The timing of any employment or professional obligations. Candidates who cannot begin the programme within the required period may not be able to take up the scholarship. Eligible Commonwealth Countries Only applicants from countries listed by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission as eligible for the Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships can apply. The eligible countries span several regions, including Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and the Pacific. Examples of eligible countries include: Africa Botswana Eswatini The Gambia Ghana Kenya Lesotho Malawi Mauritius Mozambique Namibia Nigeria Rwanda Sierra Leone South Africa Tanzania Togo Uganda Zambia Asia Bangladesh India Malaysia Maldives Pakistan Sri Lanka Caribbean and the Americas Belize Dominica Grenada Guyana Jamaica Saint Lucia Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Pacific and Small Island States Fiji Kiribati Nauru Papua New Guinea Samoa Solomon Islands Tonga Tuvalu Vanuatu The official list may also include other eligible territories and Commonwealth countries. Applicants should consult the CSC’s current eligible-country list rather than relying only on examples. The CSC has also indicated that it particularly welcomes applications from Small Island Developing States , in line with commitments associated with the 2024 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting. How the Application Process Works The Commonwealth Master’s Scholarship is an agency-nominated scholarship . This means applicants do not simply submit a direct application to the CSC and wait for consideration. Candidates must generally complete two connected application steps: Apply through the CSC’s online application system. Apply to an approved nominating agency or organisation. The CSC identifies two broad types of nominators: National nominating agencies. Selected non-governmental organisations and charitable bodies. National nominating agencies are the main application route for many candidates. Step 1: Identify the Appropriate Nominating Agency Applicants should first identify the nominating agency responsible for their country or the approved organisation through which they intend to apply. For example, the CSC lists the following nominating agency for Ghana: Registrar of Scholarships Scholarships Secretariat Accra, Ghana Applicants from Ghana should verify the latest application instructions, eligibility requirements, submission method and internal deadline directly with the Ghana Scholarships Secretariat. Each nominating agency may establish: Its own application form. Its own deadline. Additional eligibility requirements. Additional supporting documents. A national selection process. Specific subject or development priorities. Interview or screening procedures. Meeting the CSC’s general eligibility requirements does not automatically mean that an applicant meets the requirements of the nominating agency. Step 2: Apply Through CSC Central Applications to the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission are submitted through the official online application system, known as CSC Central . Applicants should create an account, complete the application form and upload the required supporting documentation before the deadline. The official CSC page advises candidates to use the save function regularly to avoid losing information. Applicants should also be aware that: Refreshing the browser window may cause them to exit the form. Unsaved information may be lost. Applications cannot be edited after submission. Applicants should use the system’s navigation buttons rather than relying on the browser’s back buttons. Clicking the CSC logo may return the user to the login screen. Two-factor authentication may be required when accessing the system. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their forms because the online system may experience heavy traffic near the deadline. There is a template application form and guidance document available to assist applicants when applying . Step 3: Apply for University Admission Applicants should also research and apply for admission to suitable UK universities and Master’s programmes. The scholarship application and university admission process are connected but separate. Applying for the scholarship does not necessarily constitute an application for admission to a university. Candidates should: Identify relevant UK universities. Review eligible taught Master’s programmes. Check academic and English-language requirements. Review tuition fees and course duration. Prepare a personal statement or study proposal where required. Apply for admission according to the university’s instructions. Seek an offer of admission as early as possible. The CSC advises applicants to seek admission to their proposed UK university at the time of, or as soon as possible after, submitting their scholarship application. Applicants should also understand that receiving a university offer does not automatically guarantee a Commonwealth Scholarship. Nominating Agencies and Their Role Nominating agencies play a central role in the Commonwealth Master’s Scholarship process. They are responsible for identifying and recommending candidates to the CSC. Each agency is allocated an agreed number of nominations and conducts its own selection process. A nominating agency may assess applicants based on: Academic performance. Leadership potential. Development impact. Professional experience. Proposed course of study. Commitment to returning or contributing to the home country. Financial need. National development priorities. Quality and clarity of the application. Because agencies may use different procedures, applicants should contact their relevant nominating body for precise instructions. There are two types of nominator invited to participate in the Master’s Scholarship programme : National nominating agencies – this is the main route of application. Selected non-governmental organisations and charitable bodies . A nomination is an important stage in the process, but it is not a guarantee that the CSC will award the scholarship. Final selection is made by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission from the pool of nominated candidates. Applicants can find general information about applying for a Commonwealth Scholarship on the advice for applicants page . Selection Process and Criteria After nominating agencies submit their candidates, the CSC reviews the applications and conducts its selection process. Applications are assessed against the Commission’s eligibility and selection requirements. Incomplete applications or applications that do not include required supporting documents may not be considered. The selection process generally considers factors such as: Academic Merit Applicants should demonstrate strong academic achievement and the ability to succeed in postgraduate study. Academic records, degree classifications and relevant qualifications may be considered when assessing academic merit. Development Impact The proposed course should be relevant to development needs. Applicants should explain how the knowledge and skills gained in the UK could contribute to their home country or wider communities. A strong application should connect: The applicant’s academic background. The proposed Master’s programme. A specific development challenge. The applicant’s future plans. The expected benefits to the home country. Leadership Potential The CSC seeks individuals who demonstrate potential to become leaders and innovators. Leadership does not necessarily mean holding a senior political or managerial position. It may be demonstrated through: Community initiatives. Research projects. Professional responsibilities. Volunteer activities. Youth development. Entrepreneurship. Public service. Advocacy. Educational work. Contributions to civil society. Applicants should provide concrete examples rather than relying only on general statements about being passionate or hardworking. Commitment to Home-Country Development Candidates should show how they intend to use their training after completing their studies. Applicants may discuss how they plan to contribute through: Public policy. Education. Healthcare. Research. Agriculture. Technology. Environmental sustainability. Governance. Economic development. Social innovation. Civil society. Private-sector development. The proposed impact should be realistic, specific and connected to the applicant’s experience and career goals. Financial Circumstances Because the scholarship is intended for candidates who cannot otherwise afford UK study, applicants may need to demonstrate their financial need. Information provided about financial circumstances should be accurate and consistent throughout the application. The Six CSC Development Themes Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships are offered under the CSC’s six development themes. Applicants should review the official themes and identify the theme that most closely relates to their proposed course and development objectives. When preparing an application, candidates should explain: Which development challenge they want to address. How their proposed Master’s programme relates to that challenge. Why UK study is relevant to their goals. How they will apply the knowledge gained. Who is likely to benefit from their future work. How their plans connect to sustainable development. Applicants should avoid selecting a development theme merely because it sounds attractive. The theme should be clearly connected to the proposed programme and the applicant’s future plans. How to Choose a Suitable UK University and Course Choosing the right university and course is an important part of the application process. Applicants should consider the following factors. Course Relevance The proposed Master’s programme should be closely related to the applicant’s academic background, professional experience or future development goals. Candidates should be able to explain why the course is necessary for their career progression and development objectives. University Strengths Applicants should research: Course content. Faculty expertise. Research centres. Practical learning opportunities. Industry and institutional partnerships. University rankings where relevant. Graduate outcomes. Student support. International student services. Rankings should not be the only deciding factor. Course relevance, academic supervision, learning structure and practical opportunities may be more important for the applicant’s objectives. Course Structure Candidates should review: Course duration. Required modules. Optional modules. Dissertation or project requirements. Assessment methods. Placement opportunities. Attendance requirements. Campus location. Start date. Applicants should ensure that the programme is a full-time taught Master’s course that meets CSC requirements. University Admission Requirements Each university may have different requirements concerning: Academic qualifications. English-language proficiency. Work experience. References. Personal statements. Transcripts. Passport documentation. Professional registration. Portfolio or writing samples. Applicants should begin checking these requirements early. Documents and Information Applicants Should Prepare The exact supporting-document requirements may vary according to the application instructions and nominating agency. However, candidates should prepare the following materials in advance where applicable: Academic certificates. University transcripts. Evidence of degree classification. Curriculum vitae or résumé. Personal statement. Study or development-impact statement. References. Proof of citizenship. Proof of permanent residence. Passport or identity document. Evidence of English-language proficiency, if required. University course information. Admission application details. Employment or professional experience information. Details of publications, awards or leadership activities. Applicants should ensure that names, dates, qualifications and employment details are consistent across all documents. Documents should be clear, authentic and uploaded in the format required by the CSC or nominating agency. Practical Advice for Preparing a Strong Application Start Early The application process involves several stages, including identifying a nominating agency, researching universities, preparing documents and completing the online form. Starting early allows applicants to address missing transcripts, request references and investigate university admission requirements. Understand Both Deadlines Applicants should distinguish between: The deadline set by their nominating agency. The final CSC application deadline. The agency deadline may be earlier. Missing the agency deadline may prevent an applicant from being nominated. Research the Course Carefully Applicants should not select a course only because the university is well known. The course should clearly support their academic interests, professional plans and development objectives. Connect the Course to a Development Challenge A strong application should explain the relationship between the proposed study and a real development issue. For example, an applicant might connect a Master’s programme to: Improving education systems. Strengthening public health. Advancing climate resilience. Promoting inclusive economic growth. Supporting digital transformation. Improving governance. Expanding access to technology. Developing agricultural productivity. Addressing gender inequality. Strengthening research and innovation. Demonstrate Evidence of Impact Applicants should provide examples of what they have already done. These examples may come from employment, research, community service, volunteering, entrepreneurship or academic projects. Instead of writing only that they are committed to development, candidates should explain: What they did. Who benefited. What challenge they addressed. What results were achieved. What they learned. How the proposed Master’s programme will build on that experience. Prepare a Realistic Future Plan Applicants should explain how they will use their training after completing the scholarship. A realistic plan may include: Returning to a current profession. Working in a relevant public institution. Developing a community initiative. Conducting research. Supporting policy development. Training other professionals. Establishing partnerships. Contributing to education or healthcare. Working with NGOs or development organisations. Check All Requirements Before Submission Before submitting the application, candidates should confirm that: They meet the citizenship requirement. They are permanently resident in an eligible country. Their academic qualifications meet the minimum standard. Their proposed course is eligible. They have applied to the relevant nominating agency. All required documents are included. Their personal statements are complete. Their references are properly arranged. Their application has been submitted before the deadline. Important Application Warnings Applicants should take note of several important points. A Nomination Is Not a Scholarship Award Being nominated by a national agency or approved organisation does not guarantee final selection. The CSC makes the final decision after assessing the nominated applications. Agency Requirements May Differ Nominating agencies may establish additional eligibility requirements or use different selection procedures. Applicants must follow both the CSC requirements and the nominating agency’s instructions. Late Applications May Not Be Accepted The CSC has stated that late applications cannot be accepted if applicants run out of time to submit their forms. Candidates should submit well before the deadline. Submitted Applications Cannot Be Edited Applicants should carefully review their forms before clicking the final submission button because applications cannot be edited after submission. Be Careful with Fraudulent Requests The CSC advises applicants to be cautious of third-party websites or individuals requesting personal information, money or supporting documentation. Applicants should use the official CSC website and official application system. Supporting documents should only be submitted through the authorised application process. The CSC has also warned that it will not ask applicants to attend in-person screening events as part of its scholarship selection process. Official Application Deadline The official deadline for Commonwealth Master’s Scholarship applications for the 2027/28 academic year is: 20 October 2026 at 16:00 BST Applications are scheduled to open on: 8 September 2026 However, applicants must confirm the deadline of their national nominating agency because agencies may require applications earlier than the CSC deadline. How to Apply Interested candidates should follow these steps: Review the official Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships information. Confirm that their country is on the eligible-country list. Identify the appropriate national nominating agency or approved organisation. Check the nominating agency’s additional requirements and internal deadline. Research eligible full-time taught Master’s programmes at UK universities. Prepare academic, personal and professional documents. Create an account on the CSC Central application system. Complete the CSC application form. Submit the required documents before the CSC deadline. Complete the separate application process required by the nominating agency. Apply for university admission as early as possible. Monitor email communications for updates. The official application information is available on the Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships page . Applicants can also review the CSC’s national nominating agencies and the official Scholarships and Fellowships section . Conclusion The Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships 2027/28 offer an important postgraduate study opportunity for talented graduates from eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries who want to pursue full-time taught Master’s degrees in the United Kingdom. Beyond academic funding, the programme is designed to strengthen professional capacity, support sustainable development and build a network of future leaders and innovators across the Commonwealth. Applicants should begin preparing early, research suitable UK courses, understand the CSC’s development themes, identify their nominating agency and carefully follow both the agency’s requirements and the CSC’s application procedures. The main CSC application deadline is 20 October 2026 at 16:00 BST , but candidates should check whether their nominating agency has an earlier deadline. A well-prepared application should clearly demonstrate academic ability, financial need, leadership potential and a realistic plan for contributing to development after completing the Master’s programme. title: Migration Policy Institute Associate Policy Analyst 2026: Apply for a Global Migration Policy Career with Worldwide Remote Work Considered
summary: The Migration Policy Institute (MPI) is accepting applications for a full-time Associate Policy Analyst – Global Program , offering an opportunity for experienced researchers and policy professionals to contribute to international migration research, comparative policy analysis, policy advising, high-level convenings, and influential publications. The position is based out of MPI’s Washington, D.C. office in the United States , but there is a particularly important provision for international applicants: remote work from anywhere in the world may be considered for the right candidate . For candidates based in the United States, the advertised starting salary is $62,000 to $67,000 per year , with final compensation depending on skills and experience. Arrangements for internationally based remote employees will be determined according to their location, experience, and applicable local employment regulations. The role sits within MPI’s Global Program , which works across some of the most consequential migration-policy issues confronting governments and societies today. Its work includes demographic change, labor markets, refugee protection, climate-related migration, international cooperation, legal migration pathways, social cohesion, and migration governance. Applications must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Wednesday, September 30, 2026 . MPI is reviewing applications on a rolling basis and specifically encourages interested candidates to apply as early as possible. About the Migration Policy Institute The Migration Policy Institute is an independent, nonpartisan, evidence-informed think tank focused on immigration, migration, and immigrant integration policy. Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Washington, D.C., MPI conducts research and policy analysis intended to improve how governments and institutions respond to migration. Its work combines empirical research, policy development, data analysis, dialogue, and the creation of practical approaches to complex migration questions. MPI works on migration issues at local, national, and international levels and examines both voluntary and forced migration. Its research spans subjects including immigration systems, refugee and asylum policy, labor markets, migration and development, integration, education, enforcement, borders, and international governance. In addition to its Washington operations, MPI has a sister organization, Migration Policy Institute Europe , headquartered in Brussels, Belgium. MPI Europe focuses particularly on migration, integration, and asylum policy within the European context. About the Associate Policy Analyst – Global Program Position The current vacancy is for a: Associate Policy Analyst – Global Program This is a full-time position designed for a professional who already has substantive research and policy experience and is ready to take an active intellectual role within MPI’s international work. The successful candidate will support the Global Program through rigorous empirical research and comparative policy analysis . Rather than functioning only as a research assistant, the Associate Policy Analyst will have opportunities to contribute ideas, participate in team strategy, help shape research methods, write publications, work on policy projects, support high-level meetings, and gradually develop an independent public research profile. MPI describes the Global Program as a highly collaborative team in which staff members are expected to contribute intellectually from the beginning. As analysts develop their expertise, there may be opportunities to co-author policy briefs, opinion pieces, and longer research publications , and eventually to single-author or lead-author some policy briefs. What Does MPI’s Global Program Do? MPI describes its Global Program as a policy laboratory that develops innovative, evidence-based, and politically feasible approaches to migration-policy challenges around the world . The program combines several forms of work: Comparative international research Policy design Direct policy advice Government engagement International cooperation Research on migration trends Stakeholder dialogue Private policy convenings Development of practical recommendations The Global Program also seeks to anticipate how major structural changes—including demographics, economic transformation, climate change, and technology—could influence migration and migration policy in the future. Its work involves governments and institutions across numerous regions, including Europe, North America, Central and South America, Africa, and the Asia-Pacific region. It also works with institutions at the European Union and United Nations levels. Geographic Scope of the Role The Global Program already has established portfolios of work in: Latin America East Africa Europe It is also developing or expanding work in: South Asia Southeast Asia Middle East North Africa Australia This international scope is one reason MPI prefers candidates with knowledge of international migration policy and expertise concerning at least one country outside the United States. Experience relating particularly to Africa, Latin America, or Europe is highlighted as desirable. Major Migration Issues the Successful Candidate Could Work On The position is deliberately broad rather than being restricted to a single migration-policy specialty. Examples provided by MPI include research concerning: Demographic Change and Labor Markets Population aging, demographic transitions, skills shortages, workforce mobility, and labor-market change are increasingly connected with migration policies. An Associate Policy Analyst may contribute to research examining how migration can interact with these demographic and economic developments. Refugee Protection The role can involve questions concerning the future of refugee and humanitarian-protection systems. MPI’s Global Program is examining how protection mechanisms can respond to increasing displacement while remaining politically and institutionally sustainable. Climate-Related Migration Climate change is increasingly influencing patterns of mobility and displacement. The Global Program examines connections between migration, resilience, development investments, and climate pressures, making climate-related mobility one of the areas relevant to the position. Legal Migration Pathways Migration systems must increasingly respond to technological change, demographic pressures, and evolving skills requirements. MPI’s Global Program has identified the design of legal pathways in this changing environment as one of its major areas of work. Public Trust and Social Cohesion The Global Program also examines how migration systems interact with public confidence, political debate, social cohesion, and rapidly changing societies. International Migration Governance Another major area involves international cooperation and the governance of migration. MPI examines how governments can coordinate migration policies, respond to crises, and create workable mechanisms for international collaboration. Five Major Pillars of MPI’s Global Program MPI identifies five principal pillars for the Global Program: Rethinking humanitarian protection systems Designing legal migration pathways in response to technological and demographic change Strengthening public trust and social cohesion around migration Using development investments to harness migration s potential and strengthen climate resilience Rethinking international cooperation and improving migration governance These areas indicate the range of research questions that an Associate Policy Analyst may encounter while working within the program. Key Duties and Responsibilities The successful candidate will be expected to perform substantial analytical and research responsibilities rather than routine administrative work. Conduct In-Depth Policy Analysis The Associate Policy Analyst will conduct detailed research and interpret evidence in ways that produce clear policy findings and practical recommendations. The role also includes helping to develop methodologies for new research projects. Draft Research Publications Writing forms a major component of the position. The successful candidate will draft and edit materials such as: Background notes Analytical reports Policy briefs Research materials Short-form analysis Longer research publications Candidates must therefore be capable of producing precise and accessible policy writing under tight deadlines and with relatively limited supervision. Contribute to MPI Publications The Associate Policy Analyst will contribute to and co-author MPI publications. As the successful candidate develops expertise and experience within the organization, there may also be opportunities to lead or independently author policy briefs. For researchers hoping to build a stronger publication record in international migration policy, this is a significant professional-development component of the role. Fundraising and Grant Management The successful applicant will also support senior staff members with fundraising and grant-management activities. Responsibilities can include: Contributing to grant proposals Assisting with grant reporting Researching potential funding opportunities Supporting broader project-development activities This means the role requires more than academic research ability. Candidates should also be comfortable working within the operational and funding structures of a nonprofit research organization. Supporting High-Level Policy Roundtables and Meetings MPI regularly brings together policymakers, researchers, government officials, and other stakeholders. The Associate Policy Analyst will help organize high-level roundtables and private meetings. Tasks may include: Developing meeting agendas Preparing concept notes Communicating with participants Briefing speakers Supporting substantive preparation for policy discussions This gives the successful candidate exposure to the practical side of policy engagement in addition to desk-based research. Potential Media Engagement MPI also states that, over time and with appropriate support, the successful candidate may engage with the news media . This could provide an opportunity to develop experience communicating research findings beyond specialist academic and policy audiences. Opportunity to Develop Your Own Research Ideas One notable feature of the position is that the new analyst is not expected merely to execute work designed entirely by senior staff. MPI states that team members are able to participate in strategy discussions and develop their own research ideas . As expertise develops, candidates may move from supporting research toward co-authoring and potentially leading policy publications. For researchers seeking to build an independent policy profile, this intellectual participation may be particularly valuable. Required Academic Qualification MPI lists the following principal qualification: A master s degree combined with three to five years of direct relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. This wording is important. It means the advertised profile is not necessarily limited exclusively to candidates who follow one rigid educational route. MPI explicitly allows an equivalent combination of education and experience . Applicants without the precise master s-plus-experience combination would therefore need to demonstrate that their alternative background provides equivalent professional preparation. Professional Experience Required Candidates should generally have approximately: 3–5 years of direct relevant experience when applying with a master s degree. Relevant experience could reasonably include work involving migration policy, international development, policy research, refugee policy, labor migration, demographic research, comparative public policy, policy analysis, or related fields, provided the experience demonstrates the capabilities requested by MPI. Applicants should avoid assuming that unrelated professional experience will automatically satisfy the requirement. Strong Research and Analytical Skills A major requirement is the ability to conduct sophisticated research and analyze substantial volumes of information. Candidates should be capable of collecting, organizing, interpreting, and synthesizing information from sources including: Primary sources Secondary sources Surveys Fieldwork Large bodies of research evidence MPI is looking for candidates who can move from collecting information to producing meaningful analytical conclusions. Quantitative Analysis Is an Advantage Experience conducting original quantitative analysis using statistical programming software is listed as an advantage. However, MPI explicitly states that this capability is not required . Applicants with skills in statistical analysis, quantitative research, programming, or data visualization should therefore highlight those capabilities, but candidates should not automatically disqualify themselves simply because their experience is predominantly qualitative. Migration Policy Expertise Candidates should understand international migration trends and policies. MPI particularly prefers candidates with substantive knowledge relating to one or more countries outside the United States , with expertise concerning Africa, Latin America, or Europe highlighted as especially relevant. This requirement aligns directly with the Global Program s comparative international mandate. A candidate with strong migration-policy expertise concerning South or Southeast Asia, MENA, Australia, or another relevant region could also be relevant given the program s expanding geographic portfolio, though the official vacancy specifically emphasizes Africa, Latin America, and Europe among preferred areas of expertise. Writing and Communication Skills Strong written and oral communication ability is essential. Candidates must be capable of taking complex empirical findings and communicating them clearly to policy and professional audiences. MPI also describes the following capabilities as advantages: Public-speaking confidence Data visualization Presenting evidence effectively Explaining data clearly to different audiences Because the position involves research publications, policy meetings, potential media engagement, and interaction with stakeholders, communication ability is central rather than secondary to the role. Ability to Manage Multiple Projects The successful candidate must be highly motivated, proactive, and capable of managing multiple assignments simultaneously. MPI s Global Program works across numerous countries, projects, funding arrangements, and policy themes. The candidate must therefore be able to: Prioritize competing assignments Maintain attention to detail Meet deadlines Switch between different kinds of work Operate in a fast-paced environment Adapt as projects evolve Intellectual Curiosity MPI also places explicit emphasis on curiosity. Candidates should be willing to read widely and incorporate ideas, approaches, and methodologies from other policy fields into migration research. The position therefore favors people who can move beyond a narrow specialty and connect migration with broader demographic, economic, political, environmental, technological, and social developments. Salary for U.S.-Based Candidates For an Associate Policy Analyst based in the United States, MPI advertises a starting salary range of: $62,000–$67,000 per year Final salary will be determined based on the candidate s skills and experience. It is important to state this precisely: the advertised $62,000–$67,000 range is specifically identified for a candidate based in the United States . International remote applicants should not assume that this exact salary range automatically applies to them. Benefits MPI states that it provides a benefits package for full-time U.S.-based employees . The vacancy page does not provide a detailed itemized list of those benefits. For international remote appointments, compensation, benefits, and employment arrangements will instead be reviewed according to: Candidate location Experience Applicable local employment laws and regulations Is This a Remote Job? Potentially, yes. The primary position is based out of Washington, D.C. , but MPI explicitly states: Remote work worldwide will be considered for the right candidate. This makes the vacancy particularly relevant to qualified migration-policy professionals outside the United States. However, “considered” should not be interpreted as a guarantee that MPI can employ a candidate in every jurisdiction. The organization states that remote employment conditions will be determined according to local employment regulations and the candidate s location. Can Applicants Outside the United States Apply? The vacancy does not impose a U.S.-only application restriction, and MPI explicitly says that worldwide remote work may be considered . Accordingly, suitably qualified candidates outside the United States can consider applying. This could potentially include applicants based in: Africa Asia Europe North America South America Australia/Oceania Middle East The decisive issues will be whether the applicant meets the professional requirements and whether a workable employment arrangement can be established under the laws applicable to their location. Applicants should not interpret the worldwide-remote language as an unconditional promise of employment from every country. Application Documents Required Applicants must submit three main documents: Cover letter Resume Short writing sample Each file should be labeled using the applicant s last name . Special 1,000-Word Writing Sample Requirement The writing sample is a particularly important part of the application. Applicants must prepare approximately: 1,000 words on an immigration policy of their choice. This provides candidates with an opportunity to demonstrate their analytical approach, command of evidence, understanding of migration policy, and ability to communicate complex policy questions concisely. A strong writing sample should ordinarily demonstrate: A clearly defined policy issue Accurate use of evidence Analytical reasoning Understanding of policy trade-offs Clear structure Concise professional writing Appropriate recommendations or implications where relevant These are practical application suggestions, rather than an additional official scoring rubric published by MPI. MPI Allows AI Tools — But Disclosure Is Required One unusual and important detail in the vacancy announcement concerns artificial intelligence. MPI explicitly states that applicants may use AI tools when preparing the writing sample , but they must disclose how those tools were used . Candidates who use AI should therefore provide transparent disclosure rather than submitting AI-assisted material without explanation. Since the purpose of the writing sample is to demonstrate the applicant s analytical and writing capability, candidates should also ensure that the final submission accurately reflects their own knowledge, reasoning, and professional judgment. Email Subject Line Applicants should use the following position title in the email subject line: Associate Policy Analyst – Global Program They must also include a line explaining how they heard about the position . Where to Send the Application Applications are submitted by email. The official careers page displays the recruitment email through protected website formatting. Independent reproductions of the same vacancy identify the recruitment address as: hr@migrationpolicy.org . Applicants should nevertheless verify the address directly on MPI s official careers page immediately before submitting their materials. Application Deadline The final application deadline is: Wednesday, September 30, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time. MPI states that applications will be assessed on a rolling basis , meaning review can begin before the final deadline. Candidates are therefore encouraged to apply early rather than assuming that submitting immediately before the deadline provides the same practical advantage as an earlier application. What Happens After Applying? MPI states that because it expects a large volume of applications, only candidates being considered for the position will be contacted . The organization also asks candidates not to make phone calls or send separate inquiries to MPI staff regarding the application. A separate listing reproducing the vacancy indicates that interviews are expected during October 2026 and that the start date is flexible but intended to occur before the end of 2026. Because these dates come from an external vacancy listing rather than the main MPI careers page, applicants should treat MPI s own communications as controlling. Application Strategy for Potential Candidates Candidates should tailor their applications carefully to the actual responsibilities of the role. A competitive cover letter should clearly demonstrate the connection between the applicant s experience and MPI s Global Program. Relevant themes to highlight may include: International migration policy Refugee and asylum policy Labor migration Migration and development Climate-related mobility Demographic change Comparative public policy International cooperation Social cohesion Migration governance Research design Policy writing Quantitative or qualitative research Stakeholder engagement Grant-funded projects Candidates should provide concrete evidence rather than simply claiming to possess these skills. For example, rather than stating “I have strong research skills,” an applicant could explain that they designed a comparative research project, analyzed survey or administrative data, produced a policy report, and presented findings to government or international stakeholders. How to Strengthen the Cover Letter Because the position is relatively specialized, a generic cover letter is unlikely to communicate the candidate s fit effectively. Applicants can consider structuring their letter around: Your Policy Expertise Briefly identify the migration-policy subjects and geographical regions in which you have developed expertise. Your Research Experience Demonstrate experience collecting and interpreting evidence, designing research, conducting fieldwork, undertaking quantitative or qualitative analysis, or preparing policy publications. Your Writing Record Highlight policy briefs, reports, academic publications, commentaries, or other relevant research outputs. Your International Perspective Because the Global Program works comparatively across countries, describe experience working across jurisdictions, cultures, or international policy environments where relevant. Your Stakeholder Experience Mention experience with government agencies, international organizations, nonprofits, universities, donors, civil-society organizations, or other policy actors if applicable. Why MPI Explain specifically why MPI s Global Program and its research agenda fit your professional background and future goals. Preparing the Writing Sample Applicants have freedom to choose an immigration policy topic. Possible areas could include: Labor migration systems Refugee resettlement Climate-related migration Skilled migration Irregular migration International student mobility Integration policy Humanitarian protection Migration-development linkages Demographic aging and immigration Border-management policy Migration agreements Talent attraction Social cohesion These are illustrative possibilities, not topics prescribed by MPI. Because the writing sample is limited to 1,000 words, candidates should focus on depth and clarity rather than attempting to cover an excessively broad policy area. Who Would This Position Be Most Relevant For? The position is particularly relevant to mid-early-career professionals who already have substantive policy or research experience. Potential applicant profiles may include: Migration policy researchers Policy analysts International-development researchers Refugee-policy specialists Migration and labor-market researchers Public-policy professionals Think-tank researchers International affairs specialists Social-science researchers Government policy professionals NGO or international-organization researchers Academics transitioning into applied policy research Eligibility should ultimately be judged against MPI s actual requirement of a master s degree plus three to five years of direct experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Equal Opportunity and Diversity MPI states that it is an Equal Opportunity Employer . The organization says it does not discriminate on the basis of: Race Gender Ethnicity Sexual or gender orientation Religion Physical ability MPI says it values a diverse working environment and welcomes applications from candidates who meet the requirements for the position. This means the vacancy does not specify a particular race or ethnicity as an eligibility condition. Key Details at a Glance Detail Information Organization Migration Policy Institute Position Associate Policy Analyst – Global Program Employment Full-time Primary office Washington, D.C., United States Remote work Worldwide remote work may be considered for the right candidate U.S.-based starting salary $62,000–$67,000 per year Main qualification Master s degree + 3–5 years of direct experience, or equivalent combination Quantitative analysis Advantage, but not mandatory Main field International migration and migration policy Application documents Cover letter, resume, 1,000-word writing sample AI in writing sample Permitted if use is disclosed Deadline September 30, 2026, 5:00 p.m. ET Review process Rolling Application method Email Recruitment email hr@migrationpolicy.org , as reproduced by current vacancy listings; verify on MPI s official page before sending The core employment, salary, qualification, application, and deadline information is confirmed by MPI s current careers page. Conclusion The Migration Policy Institute Associate Policy Analyst – Global Program position for 2026 offers a significant opportunity for experienced policy researchers who want to work at the intersection of migration research, international public policy, government engagement, and applied policy analysis. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to conduct empirical research, help develop research methodologies, contribute to influential MPI publications, support fundraising and grants, organize high-level policy discussions, and potentially engage with the media as their expertise develops. The international scope of the Global Program is particularly notable. Its work spans established projects in Latin America, East Africa, and Europe while expanding across South and Southeast Asia, MENA, and Australia. Its research addresses issues ranging from demographic shifts and labor markets to refugee protection, climate mobility, legal pathways, social cohesion, and international migration governance. Another major feature is the possibility of worldwide remote work for the right candidate . While the position is based out of Washington, D.C., qualified professionals outside the United States may be considered, with their employment terms determined according to their location, experience, and local regulations. Candidates should prepare a tailored cover letter, updated resume, and a strong 1,000-word immigration-policy writing sample. Applications are due by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on September 30, 2026 , but because applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, early submission is strongly encouraged by MPI.
